text: Hello! here I am--but no! Both the particular occasion and the general custom demand that I speak Prakrit. [_Speaking in Prakrit._] Confound it! I've been practising so long and I'm so hungry that my limbs are as weak as dried-up lotus-stalks. Suppose I go home and see whether my good wife has got anything ready or not. [_He walks about and looks around him._] Here I am at home. I'll just go in. [_He enters and looks about._] Merciful heavens! Why in the world is everything in our house turned upside down? A long stream of rice-water is flowing down the street. The ground, spotted black where the iron kettle has been rubbed clean, is as lovely as a girl with the beauty-marks of black cosmetic on her face. It smells so good that my hunger seems to blaze up and hurts me more than ever. Has some hidden treasure come to light? or am I hungry enough to think the whole world is made of rice? There surely isn't any breakfast in our house, and I'm starved to death. But everything seems topsyturvy here. One girl is preparing cosmetics, another is weaving garlands of flowers. text: "You must invite some other Brahman. I am busy." And yet I really ought to be seeking invitations from a stranger. Oh, what a wretched state of affairs! When good Charudatta was still wealthy, I used to eat my fill of the most deliciously fragrant sweetmeats, prepared day and night with the greatest of care. I would sit at the door of the courtyard, where I was surrounded by hundreds of dishes, and there, like a painter with his paint-boxes, I would simply touch them with my fingers and thrust them aside. I would stand chewing my cud like a bull in the city market. And now he is so poor that I have to run here, there, and everywhere, and come home, like the pigeons, only to roost. Now here is this jasmine-scented cloak, which Charudatta's good friend Jurnavriddha has sent him. He bade me give it to Charudatta, as soon as he had finished his devotions. text: _Vasantasena._ You mistake, sir! It is to men that treasures are entrusted, not to houses.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ Maitreya, will you receive the jewels?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Vasantasena._ I am much indebted to you. [_She hands him the jewels._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ [_Receiving them._] Heaven bless you, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ Fool! They are only entrusted to us.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside._] Then the thieves may take them, for all I care.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ In a very short time--
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ What she has entrusted to us, belongs to us.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ I shall restore them.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Vasantasena._ I should be grateful, sir, if this gentleman would accompany me home.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ Maitreya, pray accompany our guest.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ She walks as gracefully as a female swan, and you are the gay flamingo to accompany her. But I am only a poor Brahman, and wherever I go, the people will fall upon me just as dogs will snap at a victim dragged to the cross-roads.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ Very well. I will accompany her myself. Let the torches be lighted, to ensure our safety on the highway.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ Vardhamanaka, light the torches.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Vardhamanaka._ [_Aside to Maitreya._] What! light torches without oil?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside to Charudatta._] These torches of ours are like courtezans who despise their poor lovers. They won't light up unless you feed them.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Charudatta._ Enough, Maitreya! We need no torches. See, we have a lamp upon the king's highway.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: Attended by her starry servants all, And pale to see as a loving maiden's cheeks, Rises before our eyes the moon's bright ball, Whose pure beams on the high-piled darkness fall Like streaming milk that dried-up marshes seeks. 57
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [_His voice betraying his passion._] Mistress Vasantasena, we have reached your home. Pray enter. [_Vasantasena gazes ardently at him, then exit._] Comrade, Vasantasena is gone. Come, let us go home.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: All creatures from the highway take their flight; The watchmen pace their rounds before our sight; To forestall treachery, is just and right, For many sins find shelter in the night. 58
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [_He walks about._] And you shall guard this golden casket by night, and Vardhamanaka by day.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: _Maitreya._ Very well. [_Exeunt ambo._
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 30: During the mating season, a fragrant liquor exudes from the forehead of the elephant. Of this liquor bees are very fond.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 31: The most striking peculiarity of Sansthanaka's dialect--his substitution of _sh_ for _s_--I have tried to imitate in the translation.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 32: Red arsenic, used as a cosmetic.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 33: Here, as elsewhere, Sansthanaka's mythology is wildly confused. To a Hindu the effect must be ludicrous enough; but the humor is necessarily lost in a translation. It therefore seems hardly worth while to explain his mythological vagaries in detail.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 34: A name of Krishna, who is perhaps the most amorous character in Indian story.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 35: Cupid.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 36: The five deadly sins are: the slaying of a Brahman, the drinking of wine, theft, adultery with the wife of one's teacher, and association with one guilty of these crimes.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 37: These are all epithets of the same god.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [Footnote 38: Which look pretty, but do not rain. He doubtless means to suggest that the cloak, belonging to a strange man, is as useless to Vasantasena as the veil of autumn clouds to the earth.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIRST: THE GEMS ARE LEFT BEHIND

text: [_Enter a maid._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: I am sent with a message to my mistress by her mother. I must go in and find my mistress. [_She walks about and looks around her._] There is my mistress. She is painting a picture, and putting her whole heart into it. I must go and speak to her.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Then appear the love-lorn Vasantasena, seated, and Madanika._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Well, girl, and then--
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ But mistress, you were not speaking of anything. What do you mean?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Why, what did I say?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ You said, "and then"--
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Puckering her brows._] Oh, yes. So I did.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Maid._ [_Approaching._] Mistress, your mother sends word that you should bathe and then offer worship to the gods.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ You may tell my mother that I shall not take the ceremonial bath to-day. A Brahman must offer worship in my place.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Maid._ Yes, mistress. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ My dear mistress, it is love, not naughtiness, that asks the question--but what does this mean?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Tell me, Madanika. How do I seem to you?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ My mistress is so absent-minded that I know her heart is filled with longing for somebody.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Well guessed. My Madanika is quick to fathom another's heart.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ I am very, very glad. Yes, Kama is indeed mighty, and his great festival is welcome when one is young. But tell me, mistress, is it a king, or a king's favorite, whom you worship?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Girl, I wish to love, not to worship.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Is it a Brahman that excites your passion, some youth distinguished for very particular learning?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ A Brahman I should have to reverence.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Or is it some young merchant, grown enormously wealthy from visiting many cities?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ A merchant, girl, must go to other countries and leave you behind, no matter how much you love him. And the separation makes you very sad.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ It isn't a king, nor a favorite, nor a Brahman, nor a merchant. Who is it then that the princess loves?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Girl! Girl! You went with me to the park where Kama's temple stands?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Yes, mistress.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ And yet you ask, as if you were a perfect stranger.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Now I know. Is it the man who comforted you when you asked to be protected?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Well, what was his name?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Why, he lives in the merchants' quarter.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ But I asked you for his name.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ His name, mistress, is a good omen in itself. His name is Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Joyfully._] Good, Madanika, good. You have guessed it.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ [_Aside._] So much for that. [_Aloud._] Mistress, they say he is poor.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ That is the very reason why I love him. For a courtezan who sets her heart on a poor man is blameless in the eyes of the world.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ But mistress, do the butterflies visit the mango-tree when its blossoms have fallen?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ That is just why we call _that_ sort of a girl a butterfly.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Well, mistress, if you love him, why don't you go and visit him at once?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Girl, if I should visit him at once, then, because he can't make any return--no, I don't mean that, but it would be hard to see him.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Is that the reason why you left your jewels with him?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ You have guessed it.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _A voice behind the scenes_. Oh, sir, a shampooer owes me ten gold-pieces, and he got away from us. Hold him, hold him! [_To the fleeing shampooer._] Stop, stop! I see you from here. [_Enter hurriedly a frightened shampooer._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Oh, confound this gambling business!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Freed from its tether, the ace-- I might better say "ass"--how it kicks me! And the cast of the dice called the "spear" Proves true to its name; for it sticks me. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: The keeper's whole attention Was busy with the score; So it took no great invention To vanish through the door. But I cannot stand forever In the unprotected street. Is there no one to deliver? I would fall before his feet. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: While the keeper and the gambler are looking somewhere else for me, I'll just walk backwards into this empty temple and turn goddess. [_He makes all sorts of gestures, takes his place, and waits._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Enter Mathura and the gambler._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Oh, sir, a shampooer owes me ten gold-pieces, and he got away from us. Hold him, hold him! Stop, stop! I see you from here.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: You may run to hell, if they'll take you in; With Indra, the god, you may stay: For there's never a god can save your skin. While Mathura wants his pay. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Oh, whither flee you, nimble rambler. You that cheat an honest gambler? You that shake with fear and shiver. All a-tremble, all a-quiver; You that cannot trip enough. On the level ground and rough; You that stain your social station, Family, and reputation! 4
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ [_Examining the footprints._] Here he goes. And here the tracks are lost.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Gazes at the footprints. Reflectively._] Look! The feet are turned around. And the temple hasn't any image. [_After a moment's thought._] That rogue of a shampooer has gone into the temple with his feet turned around.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ Let's follow him.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ All right. [_They enter the temple and take a good look, then make signs to each other._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ What! a wooden image?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Of course not. It's stone. [_He shakes it with all his might, then makes signs._] What do we care? Come, let's have a game. [_He starts to gamble as hard as he can._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Trying with all his might to repress the gambling fever. Aside._] Oh, oh!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Oh, the rattle of dice is a charming thing, When you haven't a copper left; It works like a drum on the heart of a king, Of all his realm bereft. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: For gamblers leap down a mountain steep-- I know I shall not play. Yet the rattle of dice is as sweet as the peep Of nightingales in May. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ My turn, my turn!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Not much! it's my turn.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Coming up quickly from behind._] Isn't it _my_ turn?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ We've got our man.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Seizing him._] You jail-bird, you're caught. Pay me my ten gold-pieces.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ I'll pay you this very day.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Pay me this very minute!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ I'll pay you. Only have mercy!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Come, will you pay me now?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ My head is getting dizzy. [_He falls to the ground. The others beat him with all their might._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ There [_drawing the gamblers ring_] you're bound by the gamblers' ring.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Rises. Despairingly._] What! bound by the gamblers' ring? Confound it! That is a limit which we gamblers can't pass. Where can I get the money to pay him?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Well then, you must give surety.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ I have an idea. [_He nudges the gambler._] I'll give you half, if you'll forgive me the other half.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ All right.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_To Mathura._] I'll give you surety for a half. You might forgive me the other half.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ All right. Where's the harm?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Aloud._] You forgave me a half, sir?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Yes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_To the gambler._] And you forgave me a half?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ Yes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Then I think I'll be going.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Pay me my ten gold-pieces! Where are you going?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Look at this, gentlemen, look at this! Here I just gave surety to one of them for a half, and the other forgave me a half. And even after that he is dunning me, poor helpless me!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Seizing him._] My name is Mathura, the clever swindler, and you're not going to swindle me this time. Pay up, jail-bird, every bit of my money, and this minute, too.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ How can I pay?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Sell your father and pay.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Where can I get a father?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Sell your mother and pay.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Where can I get a mother?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Sell yourself and pay.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Have mercy! Lead me to the king's highway.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Go ahead.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ If it must be. [_He walks about._] Gentlemen, will you buy me for ten gold-pieces from this gambling-master? [_He sees a passer-by and calls out._] What is that? You wish to know what I can do? I will be your house-servant. What! he has gone without even answering. Well, here's another. I'll speak to him. [_He repeats his offer._] What! this one too takes no notice of me. He is gone. Confound it! I've had hard luck ever since Charudatta lost his fortune.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Will you pay?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ How can I pay? [_He falls down. Mathura drags him about._] Good gentlemen, save me, save me! [_Enter Darduraka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Yes, gambling is a kingdom without a throne.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: You do not mind defeat at all; Great are the sums you spend and win; While kingly revenues roll in, Rich men, like slaves, before you fall. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: You earn your coin by gambling, Your friends and wife by gambling, Your gifts and food by gambling; Your last cent goes by gambling. 8
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: My cash was taken by the trey; The deuce then took my health away; The ace then set me on the street; The four completed my defeat. 9
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_He looks before him._] Here comes Mathura, our sometime gambling-master. Well, as I can't escape, I think I'll put on my veil. [_He makes any number of gestures with his cloak, then examines it._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: This cloth is sadly indigent in thread; This lovely cloth lets in a lot of light; This cloth's protective power is nearly fled; This cloth is pretty when it's rolled up tight. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Yet after all, what more could a poor saint do? For you see,
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: One foot I've planted in the sky, The other on the ground must lie. The elevation's rather high, But the sun stands it. Why can't I? 11
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Pay, pay!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ How can I pay? [_Mathura drags him about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Well, well, what is this I see? [_He addresses a bystander._] What did you say, sir? "This shampooer is being maltreated by the gambling-master, and no one will save him"? I'll save him myself. [_He presses forward._] Stand back, stand back!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_He takes a look._] Well, if this isn't that swindler Mathura. And here is the poor saintly shampooer; a saint to be sure,
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Who does not hang with bended head Rigid till set of sun, Who does not rub his back with sand Till boils begin to run, Whose shins dogs may not browse upon, As they pass him in their rambling. Why should this tall and dainty man Be so in love with gambling? 12
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Well, I must pacify Mathura. [_He approaches._] How do you do, Mathura? [_Mathura returns the greeting._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ What does this mean?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ He owes me ten gold-pieces.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ A mere bagatelle!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Pulling the rolled-up cloak from under Darduraka's arm._] Look, gentlemen, look! The man in the ragged cloak calls ten gold-pieces a mere bagatelle.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ My good fool, don't I risk ten gold-pieces on a cast of the dice? Suppose a man has money--is that any reason why he should put it in his bosom and show it? But you,
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: You'll lose your caste, you'll lose your soul, For ten gold-pieces that he stole, To kill a man that's sound and whole, With five good senses in him. 13
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Ten gold-pieces may be a mere bagatelle to you, sir. To me they are a fortune.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Well then, listen to me. Just give him ten more, and let him go to gambling again.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ And what then?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ If he wins, he will pay you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ And if he doesn't win?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Then he won't pay you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ This is no time for nonsense. If you say that, you can give him the money yourself. My name is Mathura. I'm a swindler and I play a crooked game, and I'm not afraid of anybody. You are an immoral scoundrel.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Who did you say was immoral?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ You're immoral.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Your father is immoral. [_He gives the shampooer a sign to escape._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ You cur! That is just the way that you gamble.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ That is the way I gamble?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Come, shampooer, pay me my ten gold-pieces.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ I'll pay you this very day. I'll pay at once. [_Mathura drags him about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ Fool! You may maltreat him when I am away, but not before my eyes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Mathura seizes the shampooer and hits him on the nose. The shampooer bleeds, faints, and falls flat. Darduraka approaches and interferes. Mathura strikes Darduraka, and Darduraka strikes back._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Oh, oh, you accursèd hound! But I'll pay you for this.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ My good fool, I was walking peaceably along the street, and you struck me. If you strike me to-morrow in court, then you will open your eyes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Yes, I'll open my eyes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ How will you open your eyes?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Opening his eyes wide._] This is the way I'll open my eyes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Darduraka throws dust in Mathura's eyes, and gives the shampooer a sign to escape. Mathura shuts his eyes and falls down. The shampooer escapes._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Darduraka._ [_Aside._] I have made an enemy of the influential gambling-master Mathura. I had better not stay here. Besides, my good friend Sharvilaka told me that a young herdsman named Aryaka has been designated by a soothsayer as our future king. Now everybody in my condition is running after him. I think I will join myself to him. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Trembles as he walks away and looks about him._] Here is a house where somebody has left the side-door open. I will go in. [_He enters and perceives Vasantasena._] Madam, I throw myself upon your protection.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ He who throws himself upon my protection shall be safe. Close the door, girl. [_The maid does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ What do you fear?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ A creditor, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ You may open the door now, girl.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_To himself._] Ah! Her reasons for not fearing a creditor are in proportion to her innocence. The proverb is right:
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: The man who knows his strength and bears a load Proportioned to that strength, not more nor less, Is safe from stumbling and from sore distress, Although he wander on a dreary road. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: That means me.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Wiping his eyes. To the gambler._] Pay, pay!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ While we were quarreling with Darduraka, sir, the man escaped.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ I broke that shampooer's nose for him with my fist Come on! Let's trace him by the blood. [_They do so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ He went into Vasantasena's house, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ Then that is the end of the gold-pieces.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Gambler._ Let's go to court and lodge a complaint.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ The swindler would leave the house and escape. No, we must besiege him and so capture him.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Vasantasena gives Madanika a sign._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Whence are you, sir? or who are you, sir? or whose son are you, sir? or what is your business, sir? or what are you afraid of?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Listen, madam. My birthplace is Pataliputra, madam. I am the son of a householder. I practise the trade of a shampooer.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ It is a very dainty art, sir, which you have mastered.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Madam, as an art I mastered it. It has now become a mere trade.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Your answers are most disconsolate, sir. Pray continue.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Yes, madam. When I was at home, I used to hear travelers tell tales, and I wanted to see new countries, and so I came here. And when I had come here to Ujjayini, I became the servant of a noble gentleman. Such a handsome, courteous gentleman! When he gave money away, he did not boast; when he was injured, he forgot it. To cut a long story short: he was so courteous that he regarded his own person as the possession of others, and had compassion on all who sought his protection.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Who may it be that adorns Ujjayini with the virtues which he has stolen from the object of my mistress' desires?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Good, girl, good! I had the same thought in mind.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ But to continue, sir--
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Madam, he was so compassionate and so generous that now--
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ His riches have vanished?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ I didn't say it. How did you guess it, madam?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ What was there to guess? Virtue and money seldom keep company. In the pools from which men cannot drink there is so much the more water.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ But sir, what is his name?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Madam, who does not know the name of this moon of the whole world? He lives in the merchants' quarter. He whose name is worthy of all honor is named Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Joyfully rising from her seat._] Sir, this house is your own. Give him a seat, girl, and take this fan. The gentleman is weary. [_Madanika does as she is bid._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Aside._] What! so much honor because I mentioned Charudatta's name? Heaven bless you, Charudatta! You are the only man in the world who really lives. All others merely breathe. [_He falls at Vasantasena's feet._] Enough, madam, enough. Pray be seated, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Seating herself._] Where is he who is so richly your creditor, sir?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: The good man's wealth consists in kindly deeds; All other wealth is vain and quickly flies. The man who honors not his neighbor's needs, Does that man know what honor signifies? 15
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ But to continue--
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ So I became a servant in his employ. And when his wealth was reduced to his virtue, I began to live by gambling. But fate was cruel, and I lost ten gold-pieces.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ I am ruined! I am robbed!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ There are the gambling-master and the gambler, looking for me. You have heard my story, madam. The rest is your affair.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Madanika, the birds fly everywhither when the tree is shaken in which they have their nests. Go, girl, and give the gambling-master and the gambler this bracelet. And tell them that this gentleman sends it. [_She removes a bracelet from her arm, and gives it to Madanika._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ [_Receiving the bracelet._] Yes, mistress. [_She goes out._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ I am ruined! I am robbed!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Inasmuch as these two are looking up to heaven, and sighing, and chattering, and fastening their eyes on the door, I conclude that they must be the gambling-master and the gambler. [_Approaching._] I salute you, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ May happiness be yours.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Sir, which of you is the gambling-master?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: O maiden, fair but something less than shy, With red lip wounded in love's ardent play, On whom is bent that sweet, coquettish eye? For whom that lisp that steals the heart away? 16
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _I_ haven't got any money. You'll have to look somewhere else.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ You are certainly no gambler, if you talk that way. Is there any one who _owes_ you money?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ There is. He owes ten gold-pieces. What of him?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ In his behalf my mistress sends you this bracelet. No, no! He sends it himself.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Mathura._ [_Seizing it joyfully._] Well, well, you may tell the noble youth that his account is squared. Let him come and seek delight again in gambling. [_Exeunt Mathura and the gambler._
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ [_Returning to Vasantasena._] Mistress, the gambling-master and the gambler have gone away well-pleased.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Go, sir, and comfort your kinsfolk.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Ah, madam, if it may be, these hands would gladly practise their art in your service.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ But sir, he for whose sake you mastered the art, who first received your service, he should have your service still.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Aside._] A very pretty way to decline my services. How shall I repay her kindness? [_Aloud._] Madam, thus dishonored as a gambler, I shall become a Buddhist monk. And so, madam, treasure these words in your memory: "He was a shampooer, a gambler, a Buddhist monk."
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Sir, you must not act too precipitately.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ Madam, my mind is made up. [_He walks about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: I gambled, and in gambling I did fall, Till every one beheld me with dismay. Now I shall show my honest face to all, And walk abroad upon the king's highway. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Tumultuous cries behind the scenes._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Shampooer._ [_Listening._] What is this? What is this? [_Addressing some one behind the scenes._] What did you say? "Post-breaker, Vasantasena's rogue elephant, is at liberty!" Hurrah! I must go and see the lady's best elephant. No, no! What have I to do with these things? I must hold to my resolution. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Then enter hastily Karnapuraka, highly delighted, wearing a gorgeous mantle._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Where is she? Where is my mistress?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ Insolent! What can it be that so excites you? You do not see your mistress before your very eyes.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ [_Perceiving Vasantasena._] Mistress, my service to you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Karnapuraka, your face is beaming. What is it?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ [_Proudly._] Oh, mistress! You missed it! You didn't see Karnapuraka's heroism to-day!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ What, Karnapuraka, what?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Listen. Post-breaker, my mistress' rogue elephant, broke the stake he was tied to, killed his keeper, and ran into the street, making a terrible commotion. You should have heard the people shriek,
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: Take care of the babies, as quick as you can. And climb up a roof or a tree! The elephant rogue wants the blood of a man. Escape! Run away! Can't you see? 18
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: How they lose their ankle-rings! Girdles, set with gems and things, Break away from fastenings!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: As they stumble, trip, and blunder, See the bracelets snap asunder, Each a tangled, pearly wonder! 19
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: And that rogue of an elephant dives with his trunk and his feet and his tusks into the city of Ujjayini, as if it were a lotus-pond in full flower. At last he comes upon a Buddhist monk. And while the man's staff and his water-jar and his begging-bowl fly every which way, he drizzles water over him and gets him between his tusks. The people see him and begin to shriek again, crying "Oh, oh, the monk is killed!"
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Anxiously._] Oh, what carelessness, what carelessness!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Don't be frightened. Just listen, mistress. Then, with a big piece of the broken chain dangling about him, he picked him up, picked up the monk between his tusks, and just then Karnapuraka saw him, _I_ saw him, no, no! the slave who grows fat on my mistress' rice-cakes saw him, stumbled with his left foot over a gambler's score, grabbed up an iron pole out of a shop, and challenged the mad elephant--
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Go on! Go on!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: I hit him--in a fit of passion, too-- He really looked like some great mountain peak. And from between those tusks of his I drew The sacred hermit meek. 20
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Splendid, splendid! But go on!
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Then, mistress, all Ujjayini tipped over to one side, like a ship loaded unevenly, and you could hear nothing but "Hurrah, hurrah for Karnapuraka!" Then, mistress, a man touched the places where he ought to have ornaments, and, finding that he hadn't any, looked up, heaved a long sigh, and threw this mantle over me.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Find out, Karnapuraka, whether the mantle is perfumed with jasmine or not.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Mistress, the elephant perfume is so strong that I can't tell for sure.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Then look at the name.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Here is the name. You may read it, mistress. [_He hands her the mantle._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Reads._] Charudatta. [_She seizes the mantle eagerly and wraps it about her._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Madanika._ The mantle is very becoming to her, Karnapuraka.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ Oh, yes, the mantle is becoming enough.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Here is your reward, Karnapuraka. [_She gives him a gem._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ [_Taking it and bowing low._] Now the mantle is most wonderfully becoming.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Karnapuraka, where is Charudatta now?
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Karnapuraka._ He started to go home along this very street.
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: _Vasantasena._ Come, girl! Let us go to the upper balcony and see Charudatta. [_Exeunt omnes._
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [Footnote 39: Perhaps masseur would be more accurate.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [Footnote 40: That of Mathura, the keeper of the gambling house.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [Footnote 41: A humorously exaggerated reference to Indian ascetic practices.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [Footnote 42: See note on page 33.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [Footnote 43: The shampooer, whose transformation is astonishingly sudden.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SECOND: THE SHAMPOOER[39] WHO GAMBLED

text: [_Enter Charudatta's servant, Vardhamanaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: A master, kindly and benevolent, His servants love, however poor he be. The purse-proud, with a will on harshness bent, Pays service in the coin of cruelty. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: A bullock greedy for a feast of corn You never can prevent; A wife who wants her lord to wear a horn You never can prevent; A man who loves to gamble night and morn You never can prevent; And blemishes that with a man are born You never can prevent. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: It is some time since Charudatta went to the concert. It is past midnight, and still he does not come. I think I will go into the outer hall and take a nap. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_Enter Charudatta and Maitreya._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ How beautifully Rebhila sang! The lute is indeed a pearl, a pearl not of the ocean.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Gently the anxious lover's heart befriending, Consoling when true lovers may not meet, To love-lorn souls the dearest comforts sending, It adds to sweetest love its more of sweet. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Well then, let's go into the house.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ But how wonderfully Master Rebhila sang!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ There are just two things that always make me laugh. One is a woman talking Sanskrit, and the other is a man who tries to sing soft and low. Now when a woman talks Sanskrit, she is like a heifer with a new rope through her nose; all you hear is "soo, soo, soo." And when a man tries to sing soft and low, he reminds me of an old priest muttering texts, while the flowers in his chaplet dry up. No, I don't like it!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ My friend, Master Rebhila sang most wonderfully this evening. And still you are not satisfied.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: The notes of love, peace, sweetness, could I trace, The note that thrills, the note of passion too, The note of woman's loveliness and grace-- Ah, my poor words add nothing, nothing new! But as the notes in sweetest cadence rang, I thought it was my hidden love who sang. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: The melody of song, the stricken strings In undertone that half-unconscious clings, More clearly sounding when the passions rise, But ever sweeter as the music dies. Words that strong passion fain would say again, Yet checks their second utterance--in vain; For music sweet as this lives on, until I walk as hearing sweetest music still. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ But see, my friend! The very dogs are sound asleep in the shops that look out on the market. Let us go home. [_He looks before him._] Look, look! The blessèd moon seems to give place to darkness, as she descends from her palace in heaven.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ True.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: The moon gives place to darkness as she dips Behind the western mountain; and the tips Of her uplifted horns alone appear, Like two sharp-pointed tusks uplifted clear, Where bathes an elephant in waters cool, Who shows naught else above the jungle pool. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Well, here is our house. Vardhamanaka, Vardhamanaka, open the door!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Vardhamanaka._ I hear Maitreya's voice. Charudatta has returned. I must open the door for him. [_He does so._] Master, I salute you. Maitreya, I salute you too. The couch is ready. Pray be seated. [_Charudatta and Maitreya enter and seat themselves._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Vardhamanaka, call Radanika to wash our feet.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Compassionately._] She sleeps. Do not wake her.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Vardhamanaka._ I will bring the water, Maitreya, and you may wash Charudatta's feet.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Angrily._] Look, man. He acts like the son of a slave that he is, for he is bringing water. But he makes me wash your feet, and I am a Brahman.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Good Maitreya, do you bring the water, and Vardhamanaka shall wash my feet.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Yes, Maitreya. Do you bring the water. [_Maitreya does so. Vardhamanaka washes Charudatta's feet, then moves away._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Let water be brought for the Brahman's feet.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ What good does water do my feet? I shall have to roll in the dirt again, like a beaten ass.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Maitreya, you are a Brahman.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Yes, like a slow-worm among all the other snakes, so am I a Brahman among all the other Brahmans.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Maitreya, I will wash your feet after all. [_He does so._] Maitreya, this golden casket I was to keep by day, you by night. Take it. [_He gives it to Maitreya, then exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Receiving the casket._] The thing is here still. Isn't there a single thief in Ujjayini to steal the wretch that robs me of my sleep? Listen. I am going to take it into the inner court.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Such lax attention we can ill afford. If we are trusted by a courtezan, Then, Brahman, prove yourself an honest man, And guard it safely, till it be restored. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_He nods, repeating the stanza_ "The melody of song, the stricken strings:" _page_ 44.]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Are you going to sleep?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Yes, so it seems.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: For conquering sleep, descending on mine eyes, First smites the brow with unresisted blow; Unseen, elusive, like old age, she tries To gather strength by weakening her foe. 8
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Then let's go to sleep. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_Enter Sharvilaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: I made an entrance for my body's round By force of art and arms, a path to deeds! I skinned my sides by crawling on the ground, Like a snake that sloughs the skin no longer sound: And now I go where my profession leads. 9
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_He gazes at the sky. Joyfully._] See! The blessèd moon is setting. For well I know,
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: My trade would fain from watchmen's eyes be shrouded; Valiant, I force the dwelling of another. But see, the stars in deepest dark are clouded, And the night shields me like a careful mother. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: I made a breach in the orchard wall and entered. And now I must force my way into the inner court as well.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Yes, let men call it vulgar, if they will, The trade that thrives while sleeps the sleepyhead; Yes, knavery, not bravery, call it still, To overreach confiding folk a-bed.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Far better blame and hissing, fairly won. Than the pay of genuflecting underlings; This antique path was trod by Drona's son, Who slew the sleeping, unsuspecting kings. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: But where shall I make the breach?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Where is the spot which falling drops decayed? For each betraying sound is deadened there. No yawning breach should in the walls be made, So treatises on robbery declare. Where does the palace crumble? Where the place That niter-eaten bricks false soundness wear? Where shall I 'scape the sight of woman's face? Fulfilment of my wishes waits me there. 12
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_He feels the wall._] Here is a spot weakened by constant sun and sprinkling and eaten by saltpeter rot. And here is a pile of dirt thrown up by a mouse. Now heaven be praised! My venture prospers. This is the first sign of success for Skanda's sons. Now first of all, how shall I make the breach? The blessèd Bearer of the Golden Lance has prescribed four varieties of breach, thus: if the bricks are baked, pull them out; if they are unbaked, cut them; if they are made of earth, wet them; if they are made of wood, split them. Here we have baked bricks; ergo, pull out the bricks.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Now what shall be the shape I give the breach? A "lotus," "cistern," "crescent moon," or "sun"? "Oblong," or "cross," or "bulging pot"? for each The treatises permit. Which one? which one? And where shall I display my sovereign skill, That in the morning men may wonder still? 13
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: In this wall of baked bricks, the "bulging pot" would be effective. I will make that.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: At other walls that I have pierced by night, And at my less successful ventures too, The crowd of neighbors gazed by morning light, Assigning praise or blame, as was my due. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Praise to the boon-conferring god, to Skanda of immortal youth! Praise to him, the Bearer of the Golden Lance, the Brahman's god, the pious! Praise to him, the Child of the Sun! Praise to him, the teacher of magic, whose first pupil I am! For he found pleasure in me and gave me magic ointment,
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: With which so I anointed be, No watchman's eye my form shall see; And edged sword that falls on me From cruel wounds shall leave me free. 15
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_He anoints himself._] Alas, I have forgotten my measuring line. [_Reflecting._] Aha! This sacred cord shall be my measuring line. Yes, the sacred cord is a great blessing to a Brahman, especially to one like me. For, you see,
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: With this he measures, ere he pierce a wall, And picks the lock, when jewels are at stake. It serves as key to bolted door and hall, As tourniquet for bite of worm and snake. 16
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: The measuring is done. I begin my task. [_He does so, then takes a look._] My breach lacks but a single brick. Alas, I am bitten by a snake. [_He binds his finger with the sacred cord, and manifests the workings of poison._] I have applied the remedy, and now I am restored. [_He continues his work, then gazes._] Ah, there burns a candle. See!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Though jealous darkness hems it round, The golden-yellow candle from its place Shines through the breach upon the ground, Like a streak of gold upon the touchstone's face. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_He returns to his work._] The breach is finished. Good! I enter. But no, I will not enter yet. I will shove a dummy in. [_He does so._] Ah, no one is there. Praise be to Skanda! [_He enters and looks about._] See! Two men asleep. Come, for my own protection I will open the door. But the house is old and the door squeaks. I must look for water. Now where might water be? [_He looks about, finds water, and sprinkles the door. Anxiously._] I hope it will not fall upon the floor and make a noise. Come, this is the way. [_He puts his back against the door and opens it cautiously._] Good! So much for that. Now I must discover whether these two are feigning sleep, or whether they are asleep in the fullest meaning of the term. [_He tries to terrify them, and notes the effect._] Yes, they must be asleep in the fullest meaning of the term. For see!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Their breath first calmly rises, ere it sink; Its regularity all fear defies. Unmoving in their socket-holes, the eyes Are tightly closed, and never seem to wink. The limbs relaxed, at ease the bodies lie, I see their feet beyond the bedstead peep, The lighted candle vexes not the eye; It would, if they were only feigning sleep. 18
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_He looks about him._] What! a drum? And here is a flute. And here, a snare-drum. And here, a lute. And reed-pipes. And yonder, manuscripts. Is this the house of a dancing-master? But no! When I entered, I was convinced that this was a palatial residence. Now then, is this man poor in the fullest meaning of the term, or, from fear of the king or of thieves, does he keep his property buried? Well, my own property is buried, too. But I will scatter the seeds that betray subterranean gold. [_He does so._] The scattered seeds nowhere swell up. Ah, he is poor in the fullest meaning of the term. Good! I go.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Talking in his sleep._] Look, man. I see something like a hole in the wall. I see something like a thief. You had better take this golden casket.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Sharvilaka._ I wonder if the man has discovered that I have entered, and is showing off his poverty in order to make fun of me. Shall I kill him, or is the poor devil talking in his sleep? [_He takes a look._] But see! This thing wrapped in a ragged bath-clout, now that I inspect it by the light of my candle, is in truth a jewel-casket Suppose I take it. But no! It is hardly proper to rob a man of good birth, who is as poor as I am. I go.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ My friend, by the wishes of cows and Brahmans I conjure you to take this golden casket.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Sharvilaka._ One may not disregard the sacred wish of a cow and the wish of a Brahman. I will take it. But look! There burns the candle. I keep about me a moth for the express purpose of extinguishing candles. I will let him enter the flame. This is his place and hour. May this moth which I here release, depart to flutter above the flame in varying circles. The breeze from the insect's wings has translated the flame into accursèd darkness. Or shall I not rather curse the darkness brought by me upon my Brahmanic family? For my father was a man who knew the four Vedas, who would not accept a gift; and I, Sharvilaka, his son, and a Brahman, I am committing a crime for the sake of that courtezan girl Madanika. Now I will grant the Brahman's wish. [_He reaches out for the casket._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ How cold your fingers are, man!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Sharvilaka._ What carelessness! My fingers are cold from touching water. Well, I will put my hand in my armpit [_He warms his left hand and takes the casket._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Have you got it?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Sharvilaka._ I could not refuse a Brahman's request. I have it.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Now I shall sleep as peacefully as a merchant who has sold his wares.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Sharvilaka._ O great Brahman, sleep a hundred years! Alas that a Brahman family should thus be plunged in darkness for the sake of Madanika, a courtezan! Or better, I myself am thus plunged in darkness.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: A curse on poverty, I say! 'T is stranger to the manly will; This act that shuns the light of day I curse indeed, but do it still. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Well then, I must go to Vasantasena's house to buy Madanika's freedom. [_He walks about and looks around him._] Ah, I think I hear footsteps. I hope they are not those of policemen. Never mind. I will pretend to be a pillar, and wait. But after all, do policemen exist for me, for Sharvilaka? Why, I am
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: A cat for crawling, and a deer for flight, A hawk for rending, and a dog for sight To judge the strength of men that wake or sleep, A snake, when 't is advisable to creep, Illusion's self, to seem a saint or rogue, Goddess of Speech in understanding brogue; A light in blackest night, in holes a lizard I can be, A horse on terra firma, and a ship upon the sea. 20
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Quick as a snake, and steady as a hill; In flight the prince of birds can show no greater skill; In searching on the ground I am as keen as any hare, In strength I am a lion, and a wolf to rend and tear. 21
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ [_Entering._] Dear me! Vardhamanaka went to sleep in the outer court, and now he is not there. Well, I will call Maitreya. [_She walks about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Prepares to strike down Radanika, but first takes a look._] What! a woman? Good! I go. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ [_Recoiling in terror._] Oh, oh, a thief has cut a hole in the wall of our house and is escaping, I must go and wake Maitreya. [_She approaches Maitreya._] Oh, Maitreya, get up, get up! A thief has cut a hole in the wall of our house and has escaped.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Rising._] What do you mean, wench? "A hole in the wall has cut a thief and has escaped"?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ Poor fool! Stop your joking. Don't you see it?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ What do you mean, wench? "It looks as if a second door had been thrown open"? Get up, friend Charudatta, get up! A thief has made a hole in the wall of our house and has escaped.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Yes, yes! A truce to your jests!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ But it isn't a jest. Look!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Where?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Why, here.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Gazing._] What a very remarkable hole!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: The bricks are drawn away below, above; The top is narrow, but the center wide; As if the great house-heart had burst with pride, Fearing lest the unworthy share its love. 22
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: To think that science should be expended on a task like this!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ My friend, this hole must have been made by one of two men; either by a stranger, or else for practice by a student of the science of robbery. For what man here in Ujjayini does not know how much wealth there is in our house?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Stranger he must have been who made the breach, His customed harvest in my house to reap; He has not learned that vanished riches teach A calm, untroubled sleep.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: He saw the sometime greatness of my home And forced an entrance; for his heart did leap With short-lived hope; now he must elsewhere roam, And over broken hopes must sorely weep. 23
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Just think of the poor fellow telling his friends: "I entered the house of a merchant's son, and found--nothing."
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Do you mean to say that you pity the rascally robber? Thinks he--"Here's a great house. Here's the place to carry off a jewel-casket or a gold-casket." [_He remembers the casket. Despondently. Aside._] Where _is_ that golden casket? [_He remembers the events of the night. Aloud._] Look, man! You are always saying "Maitreya is a fool, Maitreya is no scholar." But I certainly acted wisely in handing over that golden casket to you. If I hadn't, the son of a slave would have carried it off.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ A truce to your jests!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Just because I'm a fool, do you suppose I don't even know the place and time for a jest?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ But when did this happen?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Why, when I told you that your fingers were cold.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ It might have been. [_He searches about. Joyfully._] My friend, I have something pleasant to tell you.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ What? Wasn't it stolen?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Yes.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ What is the pleasant news, then?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ The fact that he did not go away disappointed.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ But it was only entrusted to our care.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ What! entrusted to our care? [_He swoons._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Come to yourself, man. Is the fact that a thief stole what was entrusted to you, any reason why you should swoon?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Coming to himself._] Ah, my friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Who will believe the truth? Suspicion now is sure. This world will show no ruth To the inglorious poor. 24
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Alas! If envious fate before Has wooed my wealth alone. Why should she seek my store Of virtue as her own? 25
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ I intend to deny the whole thing. Who gave anybody anything? who received anything from anybody? who was a witness?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ And shall I tell a falsehood now?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: No! I will beg until I earn The wherewithal my debt to pay. Ignoble falsehood I will spurn. That steals the character away. 26
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ I will go and tell his good wife. [_She goes out, returning with Charudatta's wife._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Wife._ [_Anxiously._] Oh! Is it true that my lord is uninjured, and Maitreya too?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ It is true, mistress. But the gems which belong to the courtezan have been stolen. [_Charudatta's wife swoons._] O my good mistress! Come to yourself!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Wife._ [_Recovering._] Girl, how can you say that my lord is uninjured? Better that he were injured in body than in character. For now the people of Ujjayini will say that my lord committed this crime because of his poverty. [_She looks up and sighs._] Ah, mighty Fate! The destinies of the poor, uncertain as the water-drops which fall upon a lotus-leaf, seem to thee but playthings. There remains to me this one necklace, which I brought with me from my mother's house. But my lord would be too proud to accept it. Girl, call Maitreya hither.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ Yes, mistress. [_She approaches Maitreya._] Maitreya, my lady summons you.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Where is she?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Radanika._ Here. Come!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Approaching._] Heaven bless you!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Wife._ I salute you, sir. Sir, will you look straight in front of you?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Madam, here stands a man who looks straight in front of him.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Wife._ Sir, you must accept this.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Why?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Wife._ I have observed the Ceremony of the Gems. And on this occasion one must make as great a present as one may to a Brahman. This I have not done, therefore pray accept this necklace.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Receiving the necklace._] Heaven bless you! I will go and tell my friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Wife._ You must not do it in such a way as to make me blush, Maitreya. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_In astonishment._] What generosity!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ How Maitreya lingers! I trust his grief is not leading him to do what he ought not. Maitreya, Maitreya!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Approaching._] Here I am. Take that. [_He displays the necklace._]
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ What is this?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ Why, that is the reward you get for marrying such a wife.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ What! my wife takes pity on me? Alas, now am I poor indeed!
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: When fate so robs him of his all, That on her pity he must call, The man to woman's state doth fall, The woman is the man. 27
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: But no, I am not poor. For I have a wife
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Whose love outlasts my wealthy day; In thee a friend through good and ill; And truth that naught could take away: Ah! this the poor man lacketh still. 28
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Maitreya, take the necklace and go to Vasantasena. Tell her in my name that we have gambled away the golden casket, forgetting that it was not our own, that we trust she will accept this necklace in its place.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ But you must not give away this necklace, the pride of the four seas, for that cheap thing that was stolen before we had a bite or a drink out of it.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Not so, my friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: She showed her trust in leaving us her treasure; The price of confidence has no less measure. 29
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Friend, I conjure you by this gesture, not to return until you have delivered it into her hands. Vardhamanaka, do you speedily
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Fill up the opening with the selfsame bricks; Thus will I thwart the process of the law, For the blemish of so great a scandal sticks. 30
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: And, friend Maitreya, you must show your pride by not speaking too despondently.
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Maitreya._ How can a poor man help speaking despondently?
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: _Charudatta._ Poor I am not, my friend. For I have a wife
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Whose love outlasts my wealthy day; In thee a friend through good and ill; And truth that naught could take away: Ah, this the poor man lacketh still. (28)
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: Go then, and after performing rites of purification, I will offer my morning prayer. [_Exeunt omnes._
chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

chapter_title: ACT THE THIRD: THE HOLE IN THE WALL

text: [_Enter a maid._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: I am entrusted with a message for my mistress by her mother. Here is my mistress. She is gazing at a picture and is talking with Madanika. I will go to her. [_She walks about. Then enter Vasantasena as described, and Madanika._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Madanika girl, is this portrait really like Charudatta?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Very like.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ How do you know?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Because my mistress' eyes are fastened so lovingly upon it.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Madanika girl, do you say this because courtezan courtesy demands it?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ But mistress, is the courtesy of a girl who lives in a courtezan's house, necessarily false?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Girl, courtezans meet so many kinds of men that they do learn a false courtesy.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ But when the eyes of my mistress find such delight in a thing, and her heart too, what need is there to ask the reason?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ But I should not like to have my friends laugh at me.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ You need not be afraid. Women understand women.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ [_Approaching._] Mistress, your mother sends word that a covered cart is waiting at the side-door, and that you are to take a drive.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Tell me, is it Charudatta who invites me?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Mistress, the man who sent ornaments worth ten thousand gold-pieces with the cart--
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Is who?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Is the king's brother-in-law, Sansthanaka.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Indignantly._] Go! and never come again on such an errand.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Do not be angry, mistress. I was only sent with the message.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ But it is the message which makes me angry.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ But what shall I tell your mother?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Tell my mother never to send me another such message, unless she wishes to kill me.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ As you will. [_Exit._] [_<Enter Sharvilaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Blame for my sin I laid upon the night; I conquered sleep and watchmen of the king; But darkness wanes, and in the sun's clear light My light is like the moon's--a faded thing. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Whoever cast at me a passing look, Or neared me, anxious, as they quickly ran, All such my laden soul for foes mistook; For sin it was wherein man's fear began. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Well, it was for Madanika's sake that I did the deed of sin.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: I paid no heed to any one who talked with serving-men; The houses ruled by women-folk--these I avoided most; And when policemen seemed to have me almost in their ken, I stood stock-still and acted just exactly like a post.
