A hundred such manoeuvres did I constantly essay, And by such means succeeded in turning night to day. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_He walks about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Girl, lay this picture on my sofa and come back at once with a fan.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Yes, mistress. [_Exit with the picture._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ This is Vasantasena's house. I will enter. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: I wonder where I can find Madanika. [_Enter Madanika with the fan. Sharvilaka discovers her._] Ah, it is Madanika.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Surpassing Madana himself in charm, She seems the bride of Love, in human guise; Even while my heart the flames of passion harm, She brings a sandal coolness to my eyes. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Discovers Sharvilaka._] Oh, oh, oh, Sharvilaka! I am so glad, Sharvilaka. Where have you been?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ I will tell you. [_They gaze at each other passionately._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ How Madanika lingers! I wonder where she is. [_She looks through a bull's-eye window._] Why, there she stands, talking with a man. Her loving glance does not waver, and she gazes as if she would drink him in. I imagine he must be the man who wishes to make her free. Well, let her stay, let her stay. Never interrupt anybody's happiness. I will not call her.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Tell me, Sharvilaka. [_Sharvilaka looks about him uneasily._] What is it, Sharvilaka? You seem uneasy.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ I will tell you a secret. Are we alone?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Of course we are.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ What! a deep secret? I will not listen.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Tell me, Madanika. Will Vasantasena take a price for your freedom?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ The conversation has to do with me? Then I will hide behind this window and listen.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ I asked my mistress about it, Sharvilaka, and she said that if she could have _her_ way, she would free all her servants for nothing. But Sharvilaka, where did you find such a fortune that you can think of buying my freedom from my mistress?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: A victim to my pauper plight, And your sweet love to win, For you, my timid maid, last night I did the deed of sin. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ His face is tranquil. It would be troubled, if he had sinned.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Oh, Sharvilaka! For a mere nothing--for a woman--you have risked both things!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ What things?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Your life and your character.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ My foolish girl, fortune favors the brave.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Oh, Sharvilaka! Your character was without a stain. You didn't do anything _very_ bad, did you, when for my sake you did the deed of sin?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: The gems that magnify a woman's charm, As flowers the creeping plant, I do not harm. I do not rob the Brahman of his pelf, Nor seize the sacrificial gold myself. I do not steal the baby from the nurse, Simply because I need to fill my purse. Even as a thief, I strive with main and might For just distinction 'twixt the wrong and right. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: And so you may tell Vasantasena this:
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: These ornaments were made for you to don, Or so it seems to me; But as you love me, never put them on Where other folks may see. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ But Sharvilaka, ornaments that nobody may see, and a courtezan--the two things do not hang together. Give me the jewels. I want to see them.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Here they are. [_He gives them to her with some uneasiness._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Examining the jewels._] It seems to me I have seen these before. Tell me. Where did you get them?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ What does that matter to you, Madanika? Take them.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Angrily._] If you can't trust me, why do you wish to buy my freedom?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Well, this morning I heard in the merchants' quarter that the merchant Charudatta--
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_Vasantasena and Madanika swoon._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Madanika! Come to yourself! Why is it that now
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Your figure seems to melt in limp despair, Your eyes are wildly rolling here and there? That when I come, sweet girl, to make you free, You fall to trembling, not to pitying me? 8
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Coming to herself._] O you reckless man! When you did what you ought not to have done for my sake, you didn't kill anybody or hurt anybody in that house?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Madanika, Sharvilaka does not strike a terrified man or a man asleep. I did not kill anybody nor hurt anybody.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Really?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Really.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Recovering consciousness._] Ah, I breathe again.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Thank heaven!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Jealously._] What does this "Thank heaven" mean, Madanika?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: I sinned for you, when love had made me pine, Although my house was good since time began; Love took my virtue, but my pride is mine. _You_ call me friend and love another man? 9
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_Meaningly._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: A noble youth is like a goodly tree; His wealth, the fruit so fair; The courtezan is like a bird; for she Pecks him and leaves him bare. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Love is a fire, whose flame is lust, Whose fuel is gallantry, Wherein our youth and riches must Thus sacrificèd be. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_With a smile._] His excitement is a little out of place.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Yes!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Those men are fools, it seems to me, Who trust to women or to gold; For gold and girls, 'tis plain to see. Are false as virgin snakes and cold. 12
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Love not a woman; if you ever do, She mocks at you, and plays the gay deceiver: Yet if she loves you, you may love her too; But if she doesn't, leave her. 13
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Too true it is that
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: A courtezan will laugh and cry for gold; She trusts you not, but waits your trustful hour. If virtue and a name are yours, then hold! Avoid her as you would a graveyard flower. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: As fickle as the billows of the sea, Glowing no longer than the evening sky, A woman takes your gold, then leaves you free; You're worthless, like cosmetics, when you're dry. 15
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Yes, women are indeed fickle.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: One man perhaps may hold her heart in trust, She lures another with coquettish eyes, Sports with another in unseemly lust, Another yet her body satisfies. 16
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: As some one has well said:
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: On mountain-tops no lotuses are grown; The horse's yoke no ass will ever bear; Rice never springs from seeds of barley sown; A courtezan is not an honest fair. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Accursèd Charudatta, you shall not live! [_He takes a few steps._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Seizing the hem of his garment._] O you foolish man! Your anger is so ridiculous.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Ridiculous? how so?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Because these jewels belong to my mistress.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ And what then?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ And she left them with that gentleman.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ What for?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Whispers._] That's why.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Sheepishly._] Confound it!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: The sun was hot one summer day; I sought the shadow, there to stay: Poor fool! the kindly branch to pay, I stole its sheltering leaves away. 18
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ How sorry he seems. Surely, he did this thing in ignorance.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ What is to be done now, Madanika?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Your own wit should tell you that.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ No. For you must remember,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Nature herself gives women wit; Men learn from books a little bit. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Sharvilaka, if you will take my advice, restore the jewels to that righteous man.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ But Madanika, what if he should prosecute me?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ No cruel heat comes from the moon.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Good, Madanika, good!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Madanika,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: For what I did, I feel no grief nor fear: Why tell me of this good man's virtues high? Shame for my baseness touches me more near; What can this king do to such rogues as I? 20
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Nevertheless, your suggestion is inconsistent with prudence. You must discover some other plan.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Yes, there is another plan.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ I wonder what it will be.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Pretend to be a servant of that gentleman, and give the jewels to my mistress.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ And what then?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Then you are no thief, Charudatta has discharged his obligation, and my mistress has her jewels.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ But isn't this course too reckless?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ I tell you, give them to her. Any other course is too reckless.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Good, Madanika, good! Spoken like a free woman.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Risen at last is wisdom's light. Because I followed after you; When clouds obscure the moon by night, 'Tis hard to find a guide so true. 21
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Then you must wait here a moment in Kama's shrine, while I tell my mistress that you have come.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ I will.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Approaches Vasantasena._] Mistress, a Brahman has come from Charudatta to see you.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ But girl, how do you know that he comes from Charudatta?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Should I not know my own, mistress?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Shaking her head and smiling. Aside._] Splendid! [_Aloud._] Bid him enter.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ Yes, mistress. [_Approaching Sharvilaka._] Enter, Sharvilaka.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Approaches. With some embarrassment._] My greetings to you.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ I salute you, sir. Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ The merchant sends this message: "My house is so old that it is hard to keep this casket safe. Pray take it back." [_He gives it to Madanika, and starts to leave._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Sir, will you undertake a return commission of mine?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Aside._] Who will carry it? [_Aloud._] And this commission is--
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ You will be good enough to accept Madanika.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Madam, I do not quite understand.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ But I do.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ How so?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Charudatta told me that I was to give Madanika to the man who should return these jewels. You are therefore to understand that he makes you a present of her.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Aside._] Ah, she sees through me. [_Aloud._] Good, Charudatta, good!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: On virtue only set your heart's desire; The righteous poor attain to heights whereto The wicked wealthy never may aspire. 22
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: On virtue let the human heart be set; To virtue nothing serves as check or let The moon, attaining unattainable, is led By virtue to her seat on Shiva's head. 23
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Is my driver there? [_Enter a servant with a bullock-cart._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Servant._ Mistress, the cart is ready.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Madanika girl, you must show me a happy face. You are free. Enter the bullock-cart. But do not forget me.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Weeping._] My mistress drives me away. [_She falls at her feet._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ You are now the one to whom honor should be paid. Go then, enter the cart. But do not forget me.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Heaven bless you! and you, Madanika,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Turn upon her a happy face, And hail with bended head the grace That gives you now the name of wife. As a veil to keep you safe through life. 24
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_He enters the bullock-cart with Madanika, and starts away._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _A voice behind the scenes._ Men! Men! We have the following orders from the chief of police: "A soothsayer has declared that a young herdsman named Aryaka is to become king. Trusting to this prophecy, and alarmed thereat, King Palaka has taken him from his hamlet, and thrown him into strict confinement. Therefore be watchful, and every man at his post."
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Listening._] What! King Palaka has imprisoned my good friend Aryaka? And here I am, a married man. Confound it! But no,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Two things alone--his friend, his wife-- Deserve man's love below; A hundred brides may forfeit life Ere he should suffer so. 25
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Good! I will get out [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika._ [_Folding her hands. Tearfully._] My lord, if you must, at least bring me first to your parents.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Yes, my love. I will. I had the same thought in mind. [_To the servant._] My good fellow, do you know the house of the merchant Rebhila?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Servant._ Certainly.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Bring my wife thither.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Servant._ Yes, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Madanika_. If you desire it, dear. But dear, you must be very careful. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Sharvilaka._ Now as for me,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: I'll rouse my kin, the kitchen cabinet. Those high in fame by strength of good right arm, And those who with the king's contempt have met, And royal slaves, to save my friend from harm: Like old Yaugandharayana For the good king Udayana. 26
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: My friend has causeless been confined By wicked foes of timid kind; I fly, I fly to free him soon, Like the eclipse-oppressèd moon. [_Exit._] 27
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ [_Entering._] Mistress, I congratulate you. A Brahman has come with a message from Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Ah, this is a joyful day. Show him every mark of respect, girl, and have him conducted hither by one of the pages.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Yes, mistress. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_Enter Maitreya with a page._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ Well! Ravana, the king of the demons, travels with his chariot that they call the "Blossom." He earned it by his penances. Now I am a Brahman, and though I never performed any penances, I travel with another sort of a blossom--a woman of the town.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Sir, will you inspect our gateway.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Gazes admiringly._] It has just been sprinkled and cleaned and received a coat of green. The threshold of it is pretty as a picture with the offerings of all sorts of fragrant flowers. It stretches up its head as if it wanted to peep into the sky. It is adorned with strings of jasmine garlands that hang down and toss about like the trunk of the heavenly elephant. It shines with its high ivory portal. It is lovely with any number of holiday banners that gleam red as great rubies and wave their coquettish fingers as they flutter in the breeze and seem to invite me to enter. Both sides are decorated with holiday water-jars of crystal, which are charming with their bright-green mango twigs, and are set at the foot of the pillars that sustain the portal. The doors are of gold, thickly set with diamonds as hard to pierce as a giant's breast. It actually wearies a poor devil's envy. Yes, Vasantasena's house-door is a beautiful thing. Really, it forcibly challenges the attention of a man who doesn't care about such things.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the first court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the first court are rows of balconies brilliant as the moon, or as sea-shells, or as lotus-stalks; whitened by handfuls of powder strewn over them; gleaming with golden stairways inlaid with all sorts of gems: they seem to gaze down on Ujjayini with their round faces, the crystal windows, from which strings of pearls are dangling. The porter sits there and snoozes as comfortably as a professor. The crows which they tempt with rice-gruel and curdled milk will not eat the offering, because they can't distinguish it from the mortar. Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the second court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the second court the cart-bullocks are tied. They grow fat on mouthfuls of grass and pulse-stalks which are brought them, right and left, by everybody. Their horns are smeared with oil. And here is another, a buffalo, snorting like a gentleman insulted. And here is a ram having his neck rubbed, like a prize-fighter after the fight. And here are others, horses having their manes put in shape. And here in a stall is another, a monkey, tied fast like a thief. [_He looks in another direction._] And here is an elephant, taking from his drivers a cake of rice and drippings and oil. Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the third court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the third court are these seats, prepared for young gentlemen to sit on. A half-read book is lying on the gaming-table. And the table itself has its own dice, made out of gems. And here, again, are courtezans and old hangers-on at court, past masters in the war and peace of love, wandering about and holding in their fingers pictures painted in many colors. Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the fourth court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the fourth court the drums that maiden fingers beat are booming like the thunder; the cymbals are falling, as the stars fall from heaven when their merit is exhausted; the pipe is discoursing music as sweet as the humming of bees. And here, again, is a lute that somebody is holding on his lap like a girl who is excited by jealousy and love, and he is stroking it with his fingers. And here, again, are courtezan girls that sing as charmingly as honey-drunken bees, and they are made to dance and recite a drama with love in it. And water-coolers are hanging in the windows so as to catch the breeze. Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the fifth court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the fifth court the overpowering smell of asafetida and oil is attractive enough to make a poor devil's mouth water. The kitchen is kept hot all the time, and the gusts of steam, laden with all sorts of good smells, seem like sighs issuing from its mouth-like doors. The smell of the preparation of all kinds of foods and sauces makes me smack my lips. And here, again, is a butcher's boy washing a mess of chitterlings as if it were an old loin-cloth. The cook is preparing every kind of food. Sweetmeats are being constructed, cakes are being baked. [_To himself._] I wonder if I am to get a chance to wash my feet and an invitation to eat what I can hold. [_He looks in another direction._] There are courtezans and bastard pages, adorned with any number of jewels, just like Gandharvas and Apsarases. Really, this house is heaven. Tell me, who are you bastards anyway?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Pages._ Why, we are bastard pages--
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Petted in a stranger's court. Fed on stranger's food, Stranger's money makes us sport-- Not so very good. Stranger women gave us birth. Stranger men begot; Baby elephants in mirth, We're a bastard lot. 28
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the sixth court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the sixth court they are working in gold and jewels. The arches set with sapphires look as if they were the home of the rainbow. The jewelers are testing the lapis lazuli, the pearls, the corals, the topazes, the sapphires, the cat's-eyes, the rubies, the emeralds, and all the other kinds of gems. Rubies are being set in gold. Golden ornaments are being fashioned. Pearls are being strung on a red cord. Pieces of lapis lazuli are being cleverly polished. Shells are being pierced. Corals are being ground. Wet bundles of saffron are being dried. Musk is being moistened. Sandalwood is being ground to make sandal-water. Perfumes are being compounded. Betel-leaves and camphor are being given to courtezans and their lovers. Coquettish glances are being exchanged. Laughter is going on. Wine is being drunk incessantly with sounds of glee. Here are men-servants, here are maid-servants, and here are men who forget child and wife and money. When the courtezans, who have drunk the wine from the liquor-jars, give them the mitten, they--drink. Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the seventh court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! Here in the seventh court the mated doves are sitting comfortably in their snug dovecotes, billing and cooing and nothing else, and perfectly happy. And there is a parrot in a cage, chanting like a Brahman with a bellyful of curdled milk and rice. And here, again, is a talking thrush, chattering like a housemaid who spreads herself because somebody noticed her. A cuckoo, her throat still happy from tasting all sorts of fruit-syrups, is cooing like a procuress. Rows of cages are hanging from pegs. Quails are being egged on to fight. Partridges are being made to talk. Caged pigeons are being provoked. A tame peacock that looks as if he was adorned with all sorts of gems is dancing happily about, and as he flaps his wings, he seems to be fanning the roof which is distressed by the rays of the sun. [_He looks in another direction._] Here are pairs of flamingos like moonbeams rolled into a ball, that wander about after pretty girls, as if they wanted to learn how to walk gracefully. And here, again, are tame cranes, walking around like ancient eunuchs. Well, well! This courtezan keeps a regular menagerie of birds. Really, the courtezan's house seems to me like Indra's heaven. Show me the way, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Come, sir, and enter the eighth court.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Madam, who is this in the silk cloak, adorned with such astonishingly tautologous ornaments, who wanders about, stumbling and stretching his limbs?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Sir, this is my mistress' brother.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ What sort of ascetic exercises does a man have to perform, in order to be born as Vasantasena's brother? But no,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: He may be shiny, may be greasy, And perfumed may he be. And yet I warn you to go easy; He's a graveyard champak-tree. 29
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_He looks in another direction._] But madam, who is that in the expansive garment, sitting on the throne? She has shoes on her greasy feet.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Sir, that is my mistress' mother.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ Lord! What an extensive belly the dirty old witch has got! I suppose they couldn't put that superb portal on the house till after they had brought the idol in?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Rascal! You must not make fun of our mother so. She is pining away under a quartan ague.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Bursts out laughing._] O thou blessèd quartan ague! Look thou upon a Brahman, even upon me, with this thy favor!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Rascal! May death strike you.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Bursts out laughing._] Why, wench, a pot-belly like that is better dead.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Drinking brandy, rum, and wine, Mother fell extremely ill. If mother now should peak and pine, A jackal-pack would have its fill. 30
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Well, I have seen Vasantasena's palace with its many incidents and its eight courts, and really, it seems as if I had seen the triple heaven in a nut-shell. I haven't the eloquence to praise it. Is this the house of a courtezan, or a piece of Kubera's palace? Where's your mistress?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ She is here in the orchard. Enter, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Enters and looks about._] Well! What a beautiful orchard! There are any number of trees planted here, and they are covered with the most wonderful flowers. Silken swings are hung under the thick-set trees, just big enough for a girl to sit in. The golden jasmine, the shephalika, the white jasmine, the jessamine, the navamallika, the amaranth, the spring creeper, and all the other flowers have fallen of themselves, and really, it makes Indra's heaven look dingy. [_He looks in another direction._] And the pond here looks like the morning twilight, for the lilies and red lotuses are as splendid as the rising sun. And again:
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: The ashoka-tree, whose twigs so merry And crimson flowers have just appeared, Seems like a battling mercenary, With clotting crimson gore besmeared. 31
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Good! Now where's your mistress?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ If you would stop star-gazing, sir, you would see her.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Perceives Vasantasena and approaches._] Heaven bless you!
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Speaking in Sanskrit._] Ah, Maitreya! [_Rising._] You are very welcome. Here is a seat. Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ When you are seated, madam. [_They both seat themselves._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Is the merchant's son well?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ Well, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Tell me, good Maitreya,
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Do friends, like birds, yet seek a shelter free Beneath the modest boughs of this fair tree, Whose leaves are virtues, confidence its root, Its blossoms honor, good its precious fruit? 32
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside._] A good description by a naughty woman. [_Aloud._] They do, indeed.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Tell me, what is the purpose of your coming?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ Listen, madam. The excellent Charudatta folds his hands and requests--
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Folding her hands._] And commands--
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ He says he imagined that that golden casket was his own and gambled it away. And nobody knows where the gambling-master has gone, for he is employed in the king's business.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ Mistress, I congratulate you. The gentleman has turned gambler.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Aside._] It was stolen by a thief, and he is so proud that he says he gambled it away. I love him for that.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ He requests that you will therefore be good enough to accept in its place this necklace of pearls.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Aside._] Shall I show him the jewels? [_Reflecting._] No, not yet.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ Why don't you take this necklace?
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Laughs and looks at her friend._] Why should I not take the necklace, Maitreya? [_She takes it and lays it away. Aside._] How is it possible that drops of honey fall from the mango-tree, even after its blossoms are gone? [_Aloud._] Sir, pray tell the worthy gambler Charudatta in my name that I shall pay him a visit this evening.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside._] What else does she expect to get out of a visit to our house? [_Aloud._] Madam, I will tell him--[_Aside_ to have nothing more to do with this courtezan. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Vasantasena._ Take these jewels, girl. Let us go and bring cheer to Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: _Maid._ But mistress, see! An untimely storm is gathering.
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: The clouds may come, the rain may fall forever, The night may blacken in the sky above; For this I care not, nor I will not waver; My heart is journeying to him I love. 33
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: Take the necklace, girl, and come quickly. [_Exeunt omnes._
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 50: A name of Kama, the god of love.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 51: Used as a refrigerant.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 52: That is to say. You are now a legal wife, while I am still a courtesan.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 53: "Rams in India are commonly trained to fight." WILSON.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 54: Virtuous souls after death may become stars; but when their stellar happiness equals the sum of their acquired merit, they fall to earth again.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 55: The choristers of heaven.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 56: The nymphs of heaven.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 57: The god of wealth.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 58: This shows the excellence of Vasantasena's education. Women, as an almost invariable rule, speak Prakrit.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [Footnote 59: A gesture of respectful entreaty.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FOURTH: MADANIKA AND SHARVILAKA

text: [_The love-lorn Charudatta appears, seated._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Looks up._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: An untimely storm is gathering. For see! The peacocks gaze and lift their fans on high; The swans forget their purpose to depart; The untimely storm afflicts the blackened sky, And the wistful lover's heart. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The wet bull's belly wears no deeper dye; In flashing lightning's golden mantle clad, While cranes, his buglers, make the heaven glad, The cloud, a second Vishnu, mounts the sky. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: And yet again:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: As dark as Vishnu's form, with circling cranes To trumpet him, instead of bugle strains, And garmented in lightning's silken robe. Approaches now the harbinger of rains. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: When lightning's lamp is lit, the silver river Impetuous falls from out the cloudy womb; Like severed lace from heaven-cloaking gloom, It gleams an instant, then is gone forever. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Like shoaling fishes, or like dolphins shy, Or like to swans, toward heaven's vault that fly, Like paired flamingos, male and mate together, Like mighty pinnacles that tower on high. In thousand forms the tumbling clouds embrace, Though torn by winds, they gather, interlace, And paint the ample canvas of the sky. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The sky is black as Dhritarashtra's face; Proud as the champion of Kuru's race. The haughty peacock shrills his joy abroad; The cuckoo, in Yudhishthira's sad case, Is forced to wander if he would not die; The swans must leave their forest-homes and fly, Like Pandu's sons, to seek an unknown place. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_Reflecting._] It is long since Maitreya went to visit Vasantasena. And even yet he does not come. [_Enter Maitreya._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Confound the courtezan's avarice and her incivility! To think of her making so short a story of it! Over and over she repeats something about the affection she feels, and then without more ado she pockets the necklace. She is rich enough so that she might at least have said: "Good Maitreya, rest a little. You must not go until you have had a cup to drink." Confound the courtezan! I hope I 'll never set eyes on her again. [_Wearily._] The proverb is right. "It is hard to find a lotus-plant without a root, a merchant who never cheats, a goldsmith who never steals, a village-gathering without a fight, and a courtezan without avarice." Well, I 'll find my friend and persuade him to have nothing more to do with this courtezan. [_He walks about until he discovers Charudatta._] Ah, my good friend is sitting in the orchard. I 'll go to him. [_Approaching._] Heaven bless you! May happiness be yours.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Looking up._] Ah, my friend Maitreya has returned. You are very welcome, my friend. Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Thank you.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Tell me of your errand, my friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ My errand went all wrong.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ What! did she not accept the necklace?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ How could we expect such a piece of luck? She put her lotus-tender hands to her brow, and took it.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Then why do you say "went wrong"?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Why not, when we lost a necklace that was the pride of the four seas for a cheap golden casket, that was stolen before we had a bite or a drink out of it?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Not so, my friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: She showed her trust in leaving us her treasure; The price of confidence has no less measure. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Now look here! I have a second grievance. She tipped her friend the wink, covered her face with the hem of her dress, and laughed at me. And so, Brahman though I am, I hereby fall on my face before you and beg you not to have anything more to do with this courtezan. That sort of society does any amount of damage. A courtezan is like a pebble in your shoe. It hurts before you get rid of it. And one thing more, my friend. A courtezan, an elephant, a scribe, a mendicant friar, a swindler, and an ass--where these dwell, not even rogues are born.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Oh, my friend, a truce to all your detraction! My poverty of itself prevents me. For consider:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The horse would gladly hasten here and there, But his legs fail him, for his breath departs. So men's vain wishes wander everywhere, Then, weary grown, return into their hearts. 8
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Then too, my friend:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: If wealth is thine, the maid is thine, For maids are won by gold;
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_Aside._ And not by virtue cold. _Aloud._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: But wealth is now no longer mine, And her I may not hold. 9
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Looks down. Aside._] From the way he looks up and sighs, I conclude that my effort to distract him has simply increased his longing. The proverb is right. "You can't reason with a lover." [_Aloud._] Well, she told me to tell you that she would have to come here this evening. I suppose she isn't satisfied with the necklace and is coming to look for something else.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Let her come, my friend. She shall not depart unsatisfied. [_Enter Kumbhilaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ Listen, good people.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The more it rains in sheets, The more my skin gets wet; The more the cold wind beats, The more I shake and fret. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_He bursts out laughing._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: I make the sweet flute speak from seven holes, I make the loud lute speak on seven strings; In singing, I essay the donkey's rôles: No god can match my music when he sings. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: My mistress Vasantasena said to me "Kumbhilaka, go and tell Charudatta that I am coming." So here I am, on my way to Charudatta's house. [_He walks about, and, as he enters, discovers Charudatta._] Here is Charudatta in the orchard. And here is that wretched jackanapes, too. Well, I'll go up to them. What! the orchard-gate is shut? Good! I'll give this jackanapes a hint. [_He throws lumps of mud._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Well! Who is this pelting me with mud, as if I were an apple-tree inside of a fence?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Doubtless the pigeons that play on the roof of the garden-house.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Wait a minute, you confounded pigeon! With this stick I'll bring you down from the roof to the ground, like an over-ripe mango. [_He raises his stick and starts to run._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Holding him back by the sacred cord._] Sit down, my friend. What do you mean? Leave the poor pigeon alone with his mate.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ What! he sees the pigeon and doesn't see me? Good! I'll hit him again with another lump of mud. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Looks about him._] What! Kumbhilaka? I'll be with you in a minute. [_He approaches and opens the gate._] Well, Kumbhilaka, come in. I'm glad to see you.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ [_Enters._] I salute you, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Where do you come from, man, in this rain and darkness?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ You see, she's here.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Who's she? Who's here?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ She. See? She.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Look here, you son of a slave! What makes you sigh like a half-starved old beggar in a famine, with your "shesheshe"?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ And what makes you hoot like an owl with your "whowhowho"?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ All right. Tell me.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ [_Aside._] Suppose I say it this way. [_Aloud._] I'll give you a riddle, man.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ And I'll give you the answer with my foot on your bald spot.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ Not till you've guessed it. In what season do the mango-trees blossom?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ In summer, you jackass.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ [_Laughing._] Wrong!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside._] What shall I say now? [_Reflecting._] Good! I'll go and ask Charudatta. [_Aloud._] Just wait a moment. [_Approaching Charudatta._] My friend, I just wanted to ask you in what season the mango-trees blossom.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ You fool, in spring, in _vasanta._
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Returns to Kumbhilaka._] You fool, in spring, in _vasanta_.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ Now I 'll give you another. Who guards thriving villages?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Why, the guard.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ [_Laughing._] Wrong!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Well, I'm stuck. [_Reflecting._] Good! I'll ask Charudatta again. [_He returns and puts the question to Charudatta._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ The army, my friend, the _sena_.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Comes back to Kumbhilaka._] The army, you jackass, the _sena_.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ Now put the two together and say 'em fast.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Sena-vasanta.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ Say it turned around.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Turns around._] Sena-vasanta.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ You fool! you jackanapes! Turn the parts of the thing around!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Turns his feet around._] Sena-vasanta.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ You fool! Turn the parts of the word around!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_After reflection._] Vasanta-sena.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ She's here.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Then I must tell Charudatta. [_Approaching._] Well, Charudatta, your creditor is here.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ How should a creditor come into my family?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Not in the family perhaps, but at the door. Vasantasena is here.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Why do you deceive me, my friend?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ If you can't trust me, then ask Kumbhilaka here. Kumbhilaka, you jackass, come here.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ [_Approaching._] I salute you, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ You are welcome, my good fellow. Tell me, is Vasantasena really here?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ Yes, she's here. Vasantasena is here.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Joyfully._] My good fellow, I have never let the bearer of welcome news go unrewarded. Take this as your recompense. [_He gives him his mantle._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Kumbhilaka._ [_Takes it and bows. Gleefully._] I'll tell my mistress.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Do you see why she comes in a storm like this?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ I do not quite understand, my friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ I know. She has an idea that the pearl necklace is cheap, and the golden casket expensive. She isn't satisfied, and she has come to look for something more.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Aside._] She shall not depart unsatisfied.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_Then enter the love-lorn Vasantasena, in a splendid garment, fit for a woman who goes to meet her lover, a maid with an umbrella, and the courtier._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ [_Referring to Vasantasena._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Lakshmi without the lotus-flower is she, Loveliest arrow of god Kama's bow, The sweetest blossom on love's magic tree.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: See how she moves, so gracefully and slow! In passion's hour she still loves modesty; In her, good wives their dearest sorrow know.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: When passion's drama shall enacted be. When on love's stage appears the passing show, A host of wanderers shall bend them low. Glad to be slaves in such captivity. 12
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: See, Vasantasena, see!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The clouds hang drooping to the mountain peaks, Like a maiden's heart, that distant lover seeks: The peacocks startle, when the thunder booms, And fan the heaven with all their jeweled plumes. 13
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Mud-stained, and pelted by the streaming rain, To drink the falling drops the frogs are fain; Full-throated peacocks love's shrill passion show, And nipa flowers like brilliant candles glow; Unfaithful clouds obscure the hostage moon, Like knaves, unworthy of so dear a boon; Like some poor maid of better breeding bare, The impatient lightning rests not anywhere. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ Sir, what you say is most true. For
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The night, an angry rival, bars my way; Her thunders fain would check and hinder me: "Fond fool! with him I love thou shalt not stay, 'T is I, 't is I, he loves," she seems to say, "Nor from my swelling bosom shall he flee." 15
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ Yes, yes. That is right. Scold the night.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ And yet, sir, why scold one who is so ignorant of woman's nature! For you must remember:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The clouds may rain, may thunder ne'er so bold, May flash the lightning from the sky above; That woman little recks of heat or cold, Who journeys to her love. 16
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ But see, Vasantasena! Another cloud,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Sped by the fickle fury of the air-- A flood of arrows in his rushing streams, His drum, the roaring thunder's mighty blare, His banner, living lightning's awful gleams--
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Rages within the sky, and shows him bold 'Mid beams that to the moon allegiance owe, Like a hero-king within the hostile hold Of his unwarlike foe. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ True, true. And more than this:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: As dark as elephants, these clouds alone Fall like a cruel dart-- With streaks of lightning and with white birds strewn-- To wound my wretched heart. But, oh, why should the heron, bird of doom, With that perfidious sound Of "Rain! Rain! Rain!"--grim summons to the tomb For her who spends her lonely hours in gloom-- Strew salt upon the wound? 18
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ Very true, Vasantasena. And yet again:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: It seems as if the sky would take the guise Of some fierce elephant to service bred; The lightning like a waving streamer flies, And white cranes serve to deck his mighty head. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ But look, sir, look!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Clouds, black as wet tamala-leaves, the ball Of heaven hide from our sight; Rain-smitten homes of ants decay and fall Like beasts that arrows smite; Like golden lamps within a lordly hall Wander the lightnings bright; As when men steal the wife of some base thrall, Clouds rob the moon of light. 20
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ See, Vasantasena, see!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Clouds, harnessed in the lightning's gleams, Like charging elephants dash by; At Indra's bidding, pour their streams, Until with silver cords it seems That earth is linked with sky. 21
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: And look yonder!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: As herds of buffaloes the clouds are black; The winds deny them ease; They fly on lightning wings and little lack Of seeming troubled seas.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Smitten with falling drops, the fragrant sod, Upon whose bosom greenest grasses nod, Seems pierced with pearls, each pearl an arrowy rod. 22
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ And here is yet another cloud.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The peacock's shrill-voiced cry Implores it to draw nigh; And ardent cranes on high Embrace it lovingly.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The wistful swans espy The lotus-sweeter sky; The darkest colors lie On heaven clingingly. 23
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ True. For see!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: A thousand lotuses that bloom by night, A thousand blooming when the day is bright, Nor close nor ope their eyes to heaven's sight; There is no night nor day.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The face of heaven, thus shrouded in the night, Is only for a single instant bright, When momentary lightning gives us sight; Else is it dark alway.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Now sleeps the world as still as in the night Within the house of rain where naught is bright, Where hosts of swollen clouds seem to our sight One covering veil of gray. 24
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ True. And see!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The stars are lost like mercies given To men of evil heart; Like lonely-parted wives, the heaven Sees all her charms depart. And, molten in the cruel heat Of Indra's bolt, it seems As if the sky fell at our feet In liquid, flowing streams. 25
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: And yet again:
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The clouds first darkly rise, then darkly fall, Send forth their floods of rain, and thunder all; Assuming postures strange and manifold, Like men but newly blest with wealth untold. 26
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ True.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The heaven is radiant with the lightning's glare; Its laughter is the cry of myriad cranes; Its voice, the bolts that whistle through the air; Its dance, that bow whose arrows are the rains. It staggers at the winds, and seems to smoke With clouds, which form its black and snaky cloak. 27
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ O shameless, shameless sky!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: To thunder thus, while I To him I love draw nigh. Why do thy thunders frighten me and pain? Why am I seized upon by hands of rain? 28
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: O Indra, mighty Indra!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Did I then give thee of my love before, That now thy clouds like mighty lions roar? Ah no! Thou shouldst not send thy streaming rain, To fill my journey to my love with pain. 29
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: For Ahalya's sweet sake thou once didst lie; Thou knowest lover's pain. As thou didst suffer then, now suffer I; O cruel, cease thy rain. 30
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Thunder and rain and lighten hundredfold Forth from thy sky above; The woman canst thou not delay nor hold Who journeys to her love. 31
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Let thunders roar, for men were cruel ever; But oh, thou maiden lightning! didst thou never Know pains that maidens know? 32
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ But mistress, do not scold the lightning. She is your friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: This golden cord that trembles on the breast Of great Airavata; upon the crest Of rocky hills this banner all ablaze; This lamp in Indra's palace; but most blest As telling where your most beloved stays. 33
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ And here, sir, is his house.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ You know all the arts, and need no instruction now. Yet love bids me prattle. When you enter here, you must not show yourself too angry.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Where anger is, there love is not; Or no! except for anger hot, There is no love.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Be angry! make him angry then! Be kind! and make him kind again-- The man you love. 34
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: So much for that. Who is there? Let Charudatta know, that
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: While clouds look beautiful, and in the hour Fragrant with nipa and kadamba flower, She comes to see her lover, very wet. With dripping locks, but pleased and loving yet. Though lightning and though thunder terrifies, She comes to see you; 't is for you she sighs. The mud still soils the anklets on her feet, But in a moment she will have them sweet. 35
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Listening._] My friend, pray discover what this means.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Yes, sir. [_He approaches Vasantasena. Respectfully._] Heaven bless you!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ I salute you, sir. I am very glad to see you. [_To the courtier._] Sir, the maid with the umbrella is at your service.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Courtier._ [_Aside._] A very clever way to get rid of me. [_Aloud._] Thank you. And mistress Vasantasena,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Pride and tricks and lies and fraud Are in your face; False playground of the lustful god, Such is your face; The wench's stock in trade, in fine, Epitome of joys divine, I mean, your face-- For sale! the price is courtesy. I trust you'll find a man to buy Your face. [_Exit._] 36
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ Good Maitreya, where is your gambler?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside._] "Gambler"? Ah, she's paying a compliment to my friend. [_Aloud._] Madam, here he is in the dry orchard.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ But sir, what do you call a dry orchard?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Madam, it's a place where there's nothing to eat or drink, [_Vasantasena smiles._] Pray enter, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Aside to her maid._] What shall I say when I enter?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ "Gambler, what luck this evening?"
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ Shall I dare to say it?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ When the time comes, it will say itself.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Enter, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Enters, approaches Charudatta, and strikes him with the flowers which she holds._] Well, gambler, what luck this evening?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Discovers her._] Ah, Vasantasena is here. [_He rises joyfully._] Oh, my belovèd,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: My evenings pass in watching ever, My nights from sighs are never free; This evening cannot else than sever-- In bringing you--my grief and me. 37
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: You are very, very welcome. Here is a seat. Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Here is a seat. Be seated, madam. [_Vasantasena sits, then the others._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ But see, my friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The dripping flower that decks her ear, droops down, And one sweet breast Anointed is, like a prince who wears the crown, With ointment blest. 38
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: My friend, Vasantasena's garments are wet. Let other, and most beautiful, garments be brought.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Yes, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ Good Maitreya, do you stay here. I will wait upon my mistress. [_She does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside to Charudatta._] My friend, I'd just like to ask the lady a question.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ Then do so.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aloud._] Madam, what made you come here, when it is so stormy and dark that you can't see the moon?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ Mistress, the Brahman is very plain-spoken.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ You might better call him clever.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ My mistress came to ask how much that pearl necklace is worth.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside to Charudatta._] There! I told you so. She thinks the pearl necklace is cheap, and the golden casket is expensive. She isn't satisfied. She has come to look for something more.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ For my mistress imagined that it was her own, and gambled it away. And nobody knows where the gambling-master has gone, for he is employed in the king's business.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Madam, you are simply repeating what somebody said before.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ While we are looking for him, pray take this golden casket. [_She displays the casket._ _Maitreya hesitates._] Sir, you examine it very closely. Did you ever see it before?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ No, madam, but the skilful workmanship captivates the eye.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ Your eyes deceive you, sir. This _is_ the golden casket.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Joyfully._] Well, my friend, here is the golden casket, the very one that thieves stole from our house.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ My friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The artifice we tried before, Her stolen treasure to restore, Is practised now on us. But no, I cannot think 't is really so. 39
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ But it is so. I swear it on my Brahmanhood.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ This is welcome news.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside to Charudatta._] I'm going to ask where they found it.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ I see no harm in that.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Whispers in the maid's ear._] There!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ [_Whispers in Maitreya's ear._] So there!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ What is it? and why are we left out?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ [_Whispers in Charudatta's ear._] So there!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ My good girl, is this really the same golden casket?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ Yes, sir, the very same.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ My good girl, I have never let the bearer of welcome news go unrewarded. Take this ring as your recompense. [_He looks at his finger, notices that the ring is gone, and betrays his embarrassment._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ [_To herself._] I love you for that.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_Aside to Maitreya._] Alas,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: When in this world a man has lost his all, Why should he set his heart on longer life? His angers and his favors fruitless fall, His purposes and powers are all at strife. 40
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Like wingless birds, dry pools, or withered trees, Like fangless snakes--the poor are like to these. 41
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Like man-deserted houses, blasted trees, Like empty wells--the poor are like to these. For them no pleasant hours serve happy ends; They are forgotten of their sometime friends. 42
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ But you must not grieve thus beyond reason. [_He bursts out laughing. Aloud._] Madam, please give me back my bath-clout.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Vasantasena._ Charudatta, it was not right that you should show your distrust of me by sending me this pearl necklace.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ [_With an embarrassed smile._] But remember, Vasantasena,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Who will believe the truth? Suspicion now is sure. This world will show no ruth To the inglorious poor. 43
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Tell me, girl, are you going to sleep here to-night?
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maid._ [_Laughing._] But good Maitreya, you show yourself most remarkably plain-spoken now.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ See, my friend, the rain enters again in great streams, as if it wanted to drive people away when they are sitting comfortably together.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._ You are quite right.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The falling waters pierce the cloud, As lotus-shoots the soil; And tears the face of heaven shroud, Who weeps the moon's vain toil. 44
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: In streams as pure as thoughts to good men given, But merciless as darts that Arjun hurls, And black as Baladeva's cloak, the heaven Seems to pour out all Indra's hoarded pearls. 45
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: See, my belovèd, see!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The heaven is painted with the blackest dye, And fanned by cool and fragrant evening airs; Red lightning, glad in union, clasps the sky With voluntary arms, and shows on high The love that maiden heart to lover bears. 46
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_Vasantasena betrays her passion, and throws her arms about Charudatta. Charudatta feels her touch, and embraces her._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: More grimly yet, O thunder, boom; For by thy grace and power My love-distracted limbs now bloom Like the kadamba flower. Her dear touch all my being thrills, And love my inmost spirit fills. 47
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Maitreya._ Confound you, storm! You are no gentleman, to frighten the lady with the lightning.
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: _Charudatta._
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Do not rebuke the storm, my friend. Let ceaseless rain a hundred years endure, The lightning quiver, and the thunder peal; For what I deemed impossible is sure: Her dear-loved arms about my neck I feel. 48
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: And oh, my friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: He only knows what riches are, Whose love comes to him from afar, Whose arms that dearest form enfold, While yet with rain 't is wet and cold. 49
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Vasantasena, my belovèd,
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: The masonry is shaken; and so old The awning, that 't will not much longer hold. Heavy with water is the painted wall, From which dissolving bits of mortar fall. 50
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_He looks up._] The rainbow! See, my belovèd, see!
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: See how they yawn, the cloudy jaws of heaven, As by a tongue, by forkèd lightning riven; And to the sky great Indra's fiery bow In lieu of high-uplifted arms is given. 51
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: Come, let us seek a shelter. [_He rises and walks about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: On palm-trees shrill, On thickets still, On boulders dashing, On waters splashing, Like a lute that, smitten, sings, The rainy music rings. 52
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_Exeunt omnes._
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 60: In Indian love poetry, the rainy season is the time when lovers most ardently long to be united.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 61: In allusion to Vishnu's name, Krishna, "black."]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 62: A gesture of respect.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 63: The goddess of wealth and beauty, usually represented with a lotus.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 64: Kama's (Cupid's) arrows are flowers.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 65: Throughout this scene, Vasantasena's verses are in Sanskrit. Compare note 1 on page 73.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 66: The cry of the heron resembles the Sanskrit word for "rain." Indian love-poetry often paints the sorrow, even unto death, of her whose beloved does not return before the rainy season.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [Footnote 67: The elephant of Indra. Indra is the god of the thunderstorm.]
chapter_title: ACT THE FIFTH: THE STORM

text: [_Enter a maid._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Isn't my mistress awake yet? Well, I must go in and wake her. [_She walks about. Vasantasena appears, dressed, but still asleep. The maid discovers her._] It is time to get up, mistress. The morning is here.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Awakening._] What! is the night over? is it morning?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ For us it is morning. But for my mistress it appears to be night still.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ But girl, where is your gambler?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ Mistress, after giving Vardhamanaka his orders, Charudatta went to the old garden Pushpakaranda.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ What orders?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ To have the bullock-cart ready before daylight; for, he said, Vasantasena was to come--
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ Where, girl?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ Where Charudatta is.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Embraces the maid._] I did not have a good look at him in the evening. But to-day I shall see him face to face. Tell me, girl. Have I found my way into the inner court?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ You have found your way not only into the inner court, but into the heart of every one who lives here.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ Tell me, are Charudatta's servants vexed?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ They will be.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ When?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ When my mistress goes away.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ But not so much as I shall be. [_Persuasively._] Here, girl, take this pearl necklace. You must go and give it to my lady sister, his good wife. And give her this message: "Worthy Charudatta's virtues have won me, made me his slave, and therefore your slave also. And so I hope that these pearls may adorn your neck."
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ But mistress, Charudatta will be angry with you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ Go. He will not be angry.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ [_Takes the necklace._] Yes, mistress. [_She goes out, then returns._] Mistress, his lady wife says that her lord made you a present of it, and it would not be right for her to accept it. And further, that you are to know that her lord and husband is her most excellent adornment.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Enter Radanika, with Charudatta's little son._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ Come, dear, let's play with your little cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Rohasena._ [_Peevishly._] I don't like this little clay cart, Radanika. Give me my gold cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ [_Sighing wearily._] How should we have anything to do with gold now, my child? When your papa is rich again, then you shall have a gold cart to play with. But I'll amuse him by taking him to see Vasantasena. [_She approaches Vasantasena._] Mistress, my service to you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ I am glad to see you, Radanika. But whose little boy is this? He wears no ornaments, yet his dear little face makes my heart happy.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ This is Charudatta's son, Rohasena.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Stretches out her arms._] Come, my boy, and put your little arms around me. [_She takes him on her lap._] He looks just like his father.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ More than looks like him, he _is_ like him. At least I think so. His father is perfectly devoted to him.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ But what is he crying about?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ He used to play with a gold cart that belongs to the son of a neighbor. But that was taken away, and when he asked for it, I made him this little clay cart. But when I gave it to him, he said "I don't like this little clay cart, Radanika. Give me my gold cart."
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ Oh, dear! To think that this little fellow has to suffer because others are wealthy. Ah, mighty Fate! the destinies of men, uncertain as the water-drops which fall upon a lotus-leaf, seem to thee but playthings! [_Tearfully._] Don't cry, my child. You shall have a gold cart to play with.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Rohasena._ Who is she, Radanika?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ A slave of your father's, won by his virtues.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ My child, the lady is your mother.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS
