text: _Rohasena._ That's a lie, Radanika. If the lady is my mother, why does she wear those pretty ornaments?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ My child, your innocent lips can say terrible things. [_She removes her ornaments. Weeping._] Now I am your mother. You shall take these ornaments and have a gold cart made for you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Rohasena._ Go away! I won't take them. You're crying.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Wiping away her tears._] I'll not cry, dear. There! go and play. [_She fills the clay cart with her jewels._] There, dear, you must have a little gold cart made for you.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Exit Radanika, with Rohasena._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Enter Vardhamanaka, driving a bullock-cart._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Radanika, Radanika! Tell mistress Vasantasena that the covered cart is standing ready at the side-door.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Radanika._ [_Entering._] Mistress, Vardhamanaka is here, and he says that the cart is waiting at the side-door.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ He must wait a minute, girl, while I get ready.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Rad._ Wait a minute, Vardhamanaka, while she gets ready. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Hello, I've forgotten the cushion. I must go and get it. But the nose-rope makes the bullocks skittish. I suppose I had better take the cart along with me. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ Bring me my things, girl. I must make myself ready. [_She does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Enter, driving a bullock-cart, Sthavaraka, servant to Sansthanaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Sthavaraka._ Sansthanaka, the king's brother-in-law, said to me "Take a bullock-cart, Sthavaraka, and come as quick as you can to the old garden Pushpakaranda." Well, I'm on my way there. Get up, bullocks, get up! [_He drives about and looks around._] Why, the road is blocked with villagers' carts. What am I to do now? [_Haughtily._] Get out of my way, you! Get out of my way! [_He listens._] What's that? you want to know whose cart this is? This cart belongs to Sansthanaka, the king's brother-in-law. So get out of my way--and this minute, too! [_He looks about._] Why, here's a man going in the other direction as fast as he can. He is trying to hide like a runaway gambler, and he looks at me as if I were the gambling-master. I wonder who he is. But then, what business is it of mine? I must get there as soon as I can. Get out of my way, you villagers, get out of my way! What's that? you want me to wait a minute and put a shoulder to your wheel? Confound you! A brave man like me, that serves Sansthanaka, the king's brother-in-law, put a shoulder to your wheel? After all, the poor fellow is quite alone. I'll do it. I'll stop my cart at the side-door to Charudatta's orchard. [_He does so._] I'm coming! [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ Mistress, I think I hear the sound of wheels. The cart must be here.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ Come, girl. My heart grows impatient. Go with me to the side-door.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ Follow me, mistress.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Walks about._] You have earned a rest, girl.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Maid._ Thank you, mistress. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Feels her right eye twitch_ _as she enters the cart._] Why should my right eye twitch now? But the sight of Charudatta will smooth away the bad omen. [_Enter Sthavaraka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Sthavaraka._ I've cleared the carts out of the way, and now I'll go ahead. [_He mounts and drives away. To himself._] The cart has grown heavy. But I suppose it only seems so, because I got tired helping them with that wheel. Well, I'll go along. Get up, bullocks, get up!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _A voice behind the scenes._ Police! Police! Every man at his post! The young herdsman has just broken jail, killed the jailer, broken his fetters, escaped, and run away. Catch him! Catch him!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Enter, in excited haste, Aryaka, an iron chain on one foot. Covering his face, he walks about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Sthavaraka._ [_To himself._] There is great excitement in the city. I must get out of the way as fast as I possibly can. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: I leave behind me that accursèd sea Of human woe and human misery, The prison of the king. Like elephants that break their chains and flee, I drag a fettered foot most painfully In flight and wandering. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: King Palaka was frightened by a prophecy, took me from the hamlet where I lived, fettered me, and thrust me into a solitary cell, there to await my death. But with the help of my good friend Sharvilaka I escaped. [_He sheds tears._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: If such my fate, no sin is mine at least, That he should cage me like a savage beast. A man may fight with kings, though not with fate-- And yet, can helpless men contend with great? 2
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Whither shall I go with my wretchedness? [_He looks about._] Here is the house of some good man who hasn't locked the side-door.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: The house is old, the door without a lock, The hinges all awry. Some man, no doubt, who feels misfortune's shock As cruelly as I. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: I will enter here and wait.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _A voice behind the scenes._ Get up, bullocks, get up!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Aryaka._ [_Listening._] Ah, a bullock-cart is coming this way.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: If this should prove to be a picnic rig, Its occupants not peevishly inclined; Some noble lady's waiting carriage trig; Or rich man's coach, that leaves the town behind-- And if it empty be, fate proving kind, 'T would seem a godsend to my anxious mind. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Enter Vardhamanaka with the bullock-cart._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vardhamanaka._ There, I've got the cushion. Radanika, tell mistress Vasantasena that the cart is ready and waiting for her to get in and drive to the old garden Pushpakaranda.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Aryaka._ [_Listening._] This is a courtezan's cart, going out of the city. Good, I'll climb in. [_He approaches cautiously._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vardhamanaka._ [_Hears him coming._] Ah, the tinkling of ankle-rings! The lady is here. Mistress, the nose-rope makes the bullocks skittish. You had better climb in behind. [_Aryaka does so._] The ankle-rings tinkle only when the feet are moving, and the sound has ceased. Besides, the cart has grown heavy. I am sure the lady must have climbed in by this time. I'll go ahead. Get up, bullocks, get up! [_He drives about. Enter Viraka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Come, come! Jaya, Jayamana, Chandanaka, Mangala, Phullabhadra, and the rest of you!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: So calm, when the herdsman, slipping his tether, Breaks jail and the heart of the king together? 5
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Here! You stand at the east gate of the main street, you at the west, you at the south, you at the north. I'll climb up the broken wall here with Chandanaka and take a look. Come on, Chandanaka, come on! This way! [_Enter Chandanaka, in excitement._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Come, come! Viraka, Vishalya, Bhimangada, Dandakala, Dandashura, and the rest of you!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Come quick, my reliables! Work! Now begin! Lest the old king go out, and a new king come in. 6 Search gardens, and dives, and the town, and the street, The market, the hamlet, wherever you meet 7 With what looks suspicious. Now, Viraka, say, Who saved the young herdsman that just broke away? 8 Who was born when the sun in his eighth mansion stood, Or the moon in her fourth, or when Jupiter could Be seen in his sixth, or when Saturn was resting In his ninth, in her sixth house when Venus was nesting, Or Mars in his fifth? Who will dare to be giving The herdsman protection, while I am still living? 9, 10
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Chandanaka, you mercenary!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: I swear on your heart, he's been long out of prison, For the herdsman escaped ere the sun was half risen. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Get up, bullocks, get up!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ [_Discovers him._] Look, man, look!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: A covered cart is moving in the middle of the road; Investigate it, whose it is, and where it takes its load! 12
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ [_Discovers him._] Here, driver, stop your cart! Whose cart is this? who is in it? where is it going?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vardhamanaka._ This is Charudatta's cart. Mistress Vasantasena is in it. I am taking her to the old garden Pushpakaranda to meet Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ [_Approaches Chandanaka._] The driver says it is Charudatta's cart; that Vasantasena is in it; that he is taking her to the old garden Pushpakaranda.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Then let it pass.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Without inspection?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Certainly.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ On whose authority?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ On Charudatta's.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Who is Charudatta, or who is Vasantasena, that the cart should pass without inspection?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Don't you know Charudatta, man? nor Vasantasena? If you don't know Charudatta, nor Vasantasena, then you don't know the moon in heaven, nor the moonlight.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Who does n't know this moon of goodness, virtue's lotus-flower, This gem of four broad seas, this savior in man's luckless hour? 13 These two are wholly worshipful, our city's ornaments, Vasantasena, Charudatta, sea of excellence. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Well, well, Chandanaka! Charudatta? Vasantasena?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: I know them perfectly, as well as I know anything; But I do not know my father when I 'm serving of my king. 15
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Aryaka._ [_To himself._] In a former existence the one must have been my enemy, the other my kinsman. For see!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Their business is the same; their ways Unlike, and their desire: Like flames that gladden wedding days, And flames upon the pyre. 16
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ You are a most careful captain whom the king trusts. I am holding the bullocks. Make your inspection.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ You too are a corporal whom the king trusts. Make the inspection yourself.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ If I make the inspection, that 's just the same as if you had made it?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ If you make the inspection, that 's just the same as if King Palaka had made it.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Lift the pole, man! [_Vardhamanaka does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Aryaka._ [_To himself._] Are the policemen about to inspect me? And I have no sword, worse luck! But at least,
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Bold Bhima's spirit I will show; My arm shall be my sword. Better a warrior's death than woe That cells and chains afford. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: But the time to use force has not yet come. [_Chandanaka enters the cart and looks about._] I seek your protection.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ [_Speaking in Sanskrit._] He who seeks protection shall be safe.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Whene'er he fight, that man will suffer hurts, Will be abandoned of his friends and kin, Becomes a mock forever, who deserts One seeking aid; 't is an unpardoned sin. 18
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ What! the herdsman Aryaka? Like a bird that flees from a hawk, he has fallen into the hand of the fowler. [_Reflecting._] He is no sinner, this man who seeks my protection and sits in Charudatta's cart. Besides, he is the friend of good Sharvilaka, who saved my life. On the other hand, there are the king's orders. What is a man to do in a case like this? Well, what must be, must be. I promised him my protection just now.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: He who gives aid to frightened men, And joys his neighbor's ills to cure, If he must die, he dies; but then, His reputation is secure. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_He gets down uneasily._] I saw the gentleman--[_correcting himself_] I mean, the lady Vasantasena, and she says "Is it proper, is it gentlemanly, when I am going to visit Charudatta, to insult me on the highway?"
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Chandanaka, I have my suspicions.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Suspicions? How so?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Vir._ You gurgled in your craven throat; it seems a trifle shady. You said "I saw the gentleman," and then "I saw the lady." 20
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: That's why I'm not satisfied.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ What's the matter with you, man? We southerners don't speak plain. We know a thousand dialects of the barbarians--the Khashas, the Khattis, the Kadas, the Kadatthobilas, the Karnatas, the Karnas, the Pravaranas, the Dravidas, the Cholas, the Chinas, the Barbaras, the Kheras, the Khanas, the Mukhas, the Madhughatas, and all the rest of 'em, and it all depends on the way we feel whether we say "he" or "she," "gentleman" or "lady."
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Can't I have a look, too? It's the king's orders. And the king trusts me.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ I suppose the king doesn't trust _me_!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Is n't it His Majesty's command?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ [_Aside_] If people knew that the good herdsman escaped in Charudatta's cart, then the king would make Charudatta suffer for it. What's to be done? [_Reflecting._] I'll stir up a quarrel the way they do down in the Carnatic. [_Aloud._] Well, Viraka, I made one inspection myself--my name is Chandanaka--and you want to do it over again. Who are you?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Confound it! Who are you, anyway?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ An honorable and highly respectable person, and you don't remember your own family.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ [_Angrily._] Confound you! What is my family?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Who speaks of such things?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Speak!
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ I think I'd better not.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: I know your family, but I won't say; 'T would not be modest, such things to betray; What good's a rotten apple anyway? 21
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Speak, speak! [_Chandanaka makes a significant gesture._] Confound you! What does that mean?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: A broken whetstone in one hand--a thing That looks like scissors in the other wing-- To trim the scrubby beards that curl and cling, And you--why, you 're a captain of the king! 22
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Well, Chandanaka, you highly respectable person, you don't remember your own family either.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Tell me. What is the family I belong to, I, Chandanaka, pure as the moon?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Who speaks of such things?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Speak, speak! [_Viraka makes a significant gesture._] Confound you! What does that mean?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ Listen.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Your house is pure; your father is a drum, Your mother is a kettledrum, you scum! Your brother is a tambourine--tum, tum! And you--why, you 're a captain of the king! 23
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ [_Wrathfully._] I, Chandanaka, a tanner! You can look at the cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ You! driver! turn the cart around. I want to look in.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Vardhamanaka does so. Viraka starts to climb in. Chandanaka seizes him violently by the hair, throws him down, and kicks him._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ [_Rising. Wrathfully._] Confound you! I was peaceably going about the king's business, when you seized me violently by the hair and kicked me. So listen! If I don't have you drawn and quartered in the middle of the court-room, my name's not Viraka.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ All right. Go to court or to a hall of justice. What do I care for a puppy like you?
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Viraka._ I will. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ [_Looks about him._] Go on, driver, go on! If anybody asks you, just say "The cart has been inspected by Chandanaka and Viraka." Mistress Vasantasena, let me give you a passport. [_He hands Aryaka a sword._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS
ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Aryaka._ [_Takes it. Joyfully to himself._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: A sword, a sword! My right eye twitches fast. Now all is well, and I am safe at last. 24
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: _Chandanaka._ Madam,
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: As I have given you a passage free, So may I live within your memory. To utter this, no selfish thoughts could move; Ah no, I speak in plenitude of love. 25
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: Chandanaka is rich in virtues pure; My friend is he--Fate willed it--true and tried. I 'll not forget Chandanaka, be sure, What time the oracle is justified. 26
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: May Shiva, Vishnu, Brahma, Three in One, Protect thee, and the Moon, and blessèd Sun; Slay all thy foes, as mighty Parvati Slew Shumbha and Nishumbha--fearfully. 27
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Exit Vardhamanaka, with the bullock-cart. Chandanaka looks toward the back of the stage._] Aha! As he goes away, my good friend Sharvilaka is following him. Well, I 've made an enemy of Viraka, the chief constable and the king's favorite; so I think I too had better be following him, with all my sons and brothers.
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [Footnote 68: A bad omen, in the case of a woman.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [Footnote 69: Lalladiksita says that these horoscopes indicate respectively distress, colic, stupidity, poverty, sorrow, destruction.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [Footnote 70: A good omen, in the case of a man.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SIXTH: THE SWAPPING OF THE BULLOCK-CARTS

text: [_Enter Charudatta and Maitreya._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: How beautiful the old garden Pushpakaranda is.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ You are quite right, my friend. For see!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: The trees, like merchants, show their wares; Each several tree his blossoms bears, While bees, like officers, are flitting, To take from each what toll is fitting. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._ This simple stone is very attractive. Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ [_Seats himself._] How Vardhamanaka lingers, my friend!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._ I told Vardhamanaka to bring Vasantasena and come as quickly as he could.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Why then does he linger?
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: Is he delayed by some slow-moving load? Has he returned with broken wheel or traces? Obstructions bid him seek another road? His bullocks, or himself, choose these slow paces? 2
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: [_Enter Vardhamanaka with the bullock-cart, in which Aryaka lies hidden._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Get up, bullocks, get up!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ [_Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: And still I fear the spies that serve the king; Escape is even yet a doubtful thing, While to my foot these cursèd fetters cling.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: Some good man 't is, within whose cart I lie, Like cuckoo chicks, whose heartless mothers fly, And crows must rear the fledglings, or they die. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: I have come a long distance from the city. Shall I get out of the cart and seek a hiding-place in the grove? or shall I wait to see the owner of the cart? On second thoughts, I will not hide myself in the grove; for men say that the noble Charudatta is ever helpful to them that seek his protection. I will not go until I have seen him face to face.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: 'T will bring contentment to that good man's heart To see me rescued from misfortune's sea. This body, in its suffering, pain, and smart, Is saved through his sweet magnanimity. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Here is the garden. I 'll drive in. [_He does so._] Maitreya!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._ Good news, my friend. It is Vardhamanaka's voice. Vasantasena must have come.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Good news, indeed.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._ You son of a slave, what makes you so late?
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Don't get angry, good Maitreya. I remembered that I had forgotten the cushion, and I had to go back for it, and that is why I am late.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Turn the cart around, Vardhamanaka. Maitreya, my friend, help Vasantasena to get out.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._ Has she got fetters on her feet, so that she can't get out by herself? [_He rises and lifts the curtain of the cart._] Why, this is n't mistress Vasantasena--this is Mister Vasantasena.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ A truce to your jests, my friend. Love cannot wait. I will help her to get out myself. [_He rises._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ [_Discovers him._] Ah, the owner of the bullock-cart! He is attractive not only to the ears of men, but also to their eyes. Thank heaven! I am safe.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ [_Enters the bullock-cart and discovers Aryaka._] Who then is this?
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: As trunk of elephant his arms are long, His chest is full, his shoulders broad and strong, His great eyes restless-red; Why should this man be thus enforced to fight-- So noble he--with such ignoble plight, His foot to fetters wed? 5
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: Who are you, sir?
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ I am one who seeks your protection, Aryaka, by birth a herdsman.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Are you he whom King Palaka took from the hamlet where he lived and thrust into prison?
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ The same.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: 'T is fate that brings you to my sight; May I be reft of heaven's light, Ere I desert you in your hapless plight. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: [_Aryaka manifests his joy._]
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Vardhamanaka, remove the fetters from his foot.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Vardhamanaka._ Yes, sir. [_He does so._] Master, the fetters are removed.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ But you have bound me with yet stronger fetters of love.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Maitreya._ Now you may put on the fetters yourself. He is free anyway. And it 's time for us to be going.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Peace! For shame!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ Charudatta, my friend, I entered your cart somewhat unceremoniously. I beg your pardon.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ I feel honored that you should use no ceremony with me.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ If you permit it, I now desire to go.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ Go in peace.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ Thank you. I will alight from the cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ No, my friend. The fetters have but this moment been removed, and you will find walking difficult. In this spot where men seek pleasure, a bullock-cart will excite no suspicion. Continue your journey then in the cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ I thank you, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charud._ Seek now thy kinsmen. Happiness be thine!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ Ah, I have found thee, blessèd kinsman mine!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charud._ Remember me, when thou hast cause to speak.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ Thy name, and not mine own, my words shall seek.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charud._ May the immortal gods protect thy ways!
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ Thou didst protect me, in most perilous days.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charud._ Nay, it was fate that sweet protection lent.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ But thou wast chosen as fate's instrument. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Charudatta._ King Palaka is aroused, and protection will prove difficult. You must depart at once.
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: _Aryaka._ Until we meet again, farewell. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: From royal wrath I now have much to fear; It were unwise for me to linger here. Then throw the fetters in the well; for spies Serve to their king as keen, far-seeing eyes. 8
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: [_His left eye twitches._] Maitreya, my friend, I long to see Vasantasena. For now, because
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: I have not seen whom I love best, My left eye twitches; and my breast Is causeless-anxious and distressed. 9
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: Come, let us go. [_He walks about._] See! a Buddhist monk approaches, and the sight bodes ill. [_Reflecting._] Let him enter by that path, while we depart by this. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: [Footnote 71: Lalladiksita says that these are signs of royalty.]
chapter_title: ACT THE SEVENTH: ARYAKA'S ESCAPE

text: [_Enter a monk, with a wet garment in his hand._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Ye ignorant, lay by a store of virtue! Restrain the belly; watch eternally, Heeding the beat of contemplation's drum, For else the senses--fearful thieves they be-- Will steal away all virtue's hoarded sum. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: And further: I have seen that all things are transitory, so that now I am become the abode of virtues alone.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Who slays the Five Men, and the Female Bane, By whom protection to the Town is given, By whom the Outcaste impotent is slain, He cannot fail to enter into heaven. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Though head be shorn and face be shorn, The heart unshorn, why should man shave him? But he whose inmost heart is shorn Needs not the shaven head to save him. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: I have dyed this robe of mine yellow. And now I will go into the garden of the king's brother-in-law, wash it in the pond, and go away as soon as I can. [_He walks about and washes the robe._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _A voice behind the scenes._ Shtop, you confounded monk, shtop!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ [_Discovers the speaker. Fearfully._ ] Heaven help me! Here is the king's brother-in-law, Sansthanaka. Just because one monk committed an offense, now, wherever he sees a monk, whether it is the same one or not, he bores a hole in his nose and drives him around like a bullock. Where shall a defenseless man find a defender? But after all, the blessèd Lord Buddha is my defender.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Enter the courtier, carrying a sword, and Sansthanaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Shtop, you confounded monk, shtop! I'll pound your head like a red radish at a drinking party. [_He strikes him._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ You jackass, you should not strike a monk who wears the yellow robes of renunciation. Why heed him? Look rather upon this garden, which offers itself to pleasure.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: To creatures else forlorn, the forest trees Do works of mercy, granting joy and ease; Like a sinner's heart, the park unguarded lies, Like some new-founded realm, an easy prize. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ Heaven bless you! Be merciful, servant of the Blessèd One!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Did you hear that, shir? He's inshulting me.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ What does he say?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Shays I'm a shervant. What do you take me for? a barber?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ A servant of the Blessèd One he calls you, and this is praise.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Praise me shome more, monk!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ You are virtuous! You are a brick!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Shee? He shays I'm virtuous. He shays I'm a brick. What do you think I am? a materialistic philosopher? or a watering-trough? or a pot-maker?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ You jackass, he praises you when he says that you are virtuous, that you are a brick.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Well, shir, what did he come here for?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ To wash this robe.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Confound the monk! My shishter's husband gave me the finesht garden there is, the garden Pushpakaranda. Dogs and jackals drink the water in thish pond. Now I'm an arishtocrat. I'm a man, and I don't even take a bath. And here you bring your shtinking clothes, all shtained with shtale bean-porridge, and wash 'em! I think one good shtroke will finish you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ You jackass, I am sure he has not long been a monk.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ How can you tell, shir?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ It doesn't take much to tell that, See!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: His hair is newly shorn; the brow still white; The rough cloak has not yet the shoulder scarred; He wears it awkwardly; it clings not tight; And here above, the fit is sadly marred. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ True, servant of the Blessèd One. I have been a monk but a short time.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Then why haven't you been one all your life? [_He beats him._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ Buddha be praised!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Stop beating the poor fellow. Leave him alone. Let him go.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Jusht wait a minute, while I take counshel.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ With whom?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ With my own heart.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Poor fellow! Why didn't he escape?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Blesshèd little heart, my little shon and mashter, shall the monk go, or shall the monk shtay? [_To himself._] Neither go, nor shtay. [_Aloud._] Well, shir, I took counshel with my heart, and my heart shays--
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Says what?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ He shall neither go, nor shtay. He shall neither breathe up, nor breathe down. He shall fall down right here and die, before you can shay "boo."
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ Buddha be praised! I throw myself upon your protection.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Let him go.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Well, on one condition.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ And what is that?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ He musht shling mud in, without making the water dirty. Or better yet, he musht make the water into a ball, and shling it into the mud.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ What incredible folly!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The patient earth is burdened by So many a fool, so many a drone, Whose thoughts and deeds are all awry-- These trees of flesh, these forms of stone. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_The monk makes faces at Sansthanaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ What does he mean?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ He praises you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Praise me shome more! Praise me again! [_The monk does so, then exit._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ See how beautiful the garden is, you jackass.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: See yonder trees, adorned with fruit and flowers, O'er which the clinging creepers interlace; The watchmen guard them with the royal powers; They seem like men whom loving wives embrace. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ A good deshcription, shir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The ground is mottled with a lot of flowers; The blosshom freight bends down the lofty trees; And, hanging from the leafy tree-top bowers, The monkeys bob, like breadfruit in the breeze. 8
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Will you be seated on this stone bench, you jackass?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I am sheated. [_They seat themselves._] Do you know, shir, I remember that Vasantasena even yet. She is like an inshult. I can't get her out of my mind.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Aside._] He remembers her even after such a repulse. For indeed,
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The mean man, whom a woman spurns, But loves the more; The wise man's passion gentler burns, Or passes o'er. 9
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Shome time has passhed, shir, shince I told my shervant Sthavaraka to take the bullock-cart and come as quick as he could. And even yet he is not here. I 've been hungry a long time, and at noon a man can't go a-foot. For shee!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The shun is in the middle of the shky, And hard to look at as an angry ape; Like Gandhari, whose hundred shons did die, The earth is hard dishtresshed and can't eshcape. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ True.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The cattle all--their cuds let fall-- Lie drowsing in the shade; In heated pool their lips to cool, Deer throng the woodland glade; A prey to heat, the city street Makes wanderers afraid; The cart must shun the midday sun, And thus has been delayed. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Yesshir,
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Fasht to my head the heated shun-beam clings; Birds, flying creatures, alsho wingèd things Resht in the branches of the trees, while men, People, and pershons shigh and shigh again; At home they tarry, in their houses shtay, To bear the heat and burden of the day. 12
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Well, shir, that shervant is n't here yet. I 'm going to shing shomething to passh the time. [_He sings._] There, shir, did you hear what I shang?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ What shall I say? Ah, how melodious!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Why _should n't_ it be malodorous?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Of nut-grass and cumin I make up a pickle, Of devil's-dung, ginger, and orris, and treacle; That's the mixture of perfumes I eagerly eat; Why should n't my voice be remarkably shweet? 13
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Well, shir, I 'm jusht going to shing again, [_He does so._] There, shir, did you hear what I shang?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ What shall I say? Ah, how melodious!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Why _should n't_ it be malodorous?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Of the flesh of the cuckoo I make up a chowder, With devil's-dung added, and black pepper powder; With oil and with butter I shprinkle the meat: Why should n't my voice be remarkably shweet? 14
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: But shir, the shervant is n't here yet.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Be easy in your mind. He will be here presently.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Enter Vasantasena in the bullock-cart, and Sthavaraka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ I 'm frightened. It is already noon. I hope Sansthanaka, the king's brother-in-law, will not be angry. I must drive faster. Get up, bullocks, get up!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Alas! That is not Vardhamanaka's voice. What does it mean? I wonder if Charudatta was afraid that the bullocks might become weary, and so sent another man with another cart. My right eye twitches. My heart is all a-tremble. There is no one in sight. Everything seems to dance before my eyes.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Hearing the sound of wheels._] The cart is here, shir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ How do you know?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Can't you shee? It shqueaks like an old hog.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Perceives the cart._] Quite true. It is here.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Sthavaraka, my little shon, my shlave, are you here?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Yes, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Is the cart here?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Yes, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Are the bullocks here?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Yes, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ And are you here?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ [_Laughing._] Yes, master, I am here too.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Then drive the cart in.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ By which road?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Right here, where the wall is tumbling down.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Oh, master, the bullocks will be killed. The cart will go to pieces. And I, your servant, shall be killed.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I'm the king's brother-in-law, man. If the bullocks are killed, I 'll buy shome more. If the cart goes to pieces, I 'll have another one made. If you are killed, there will be another driver.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Everything will be replaced--except me.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Let the whole thing go to pieces. Drive in over the wall.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Then break, cart, break with your driver. There will be another cart. I must go and present myself to my master. [_He drives in._] What! not broken? Master, here is your cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ The bullocks not shplit in two? and the ropes not killed? and you too not killed?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ No, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Come, shir. Let's look at the cart. You are my teacher, shir, my very besht teacher. You are a man I reshpect, my intimate friend, a man I delight to honor. Do you enter the cart firsht.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Very well. [_He starts to do so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Not much! Shtop! Is thish your father's cart, that you should enter it firsht? I own thish cart. I 'll enter it firsht.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ I only did what you said.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Even if I do shay sho, you ought to be polite enough to shay "After you, mashter."
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ After you, then.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Now I 'll enter. Sthavaraka, my little shon, my shlave, turn the cart around.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ [_Does so._] Enter, master.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Enters and looks about, then hastily gets out in terror, and falls on the courtier's neck._] Oh, oh, oh! You're a dead man! There's a witch, or a thief, that's sitting and living in my bullock-cart. If it's a witch, we 'll both be robbed. If it's a thief, we 'll both be eaten alive.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Don't be frightened. How could a witch travel in a bullock-cart? I hope that the heat of the midday sun has not blinded you, so that you became the victim of an hallucination when you saw the shadow of Sthavaraka with the smock on it.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Sthavaraka, my little shon, my shlave, are you alive?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Yes, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ But shir, there's a woman sitting and living in the bullock-cart. Look and shee!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ A woman?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Then let us bow our heads at once and go, Like steers whose eyes the falling raindrops daze; In public spots my dignity I show; On high-born dames I hesitate to gaze. 15
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_In amazement. Aside._] Oh, oh! It is that thorn in my eye, the king's brother-in-law. Alas! the danger is great. Poor woman! My coming hither proves as fruitless as the sowing of a handful of seeds on salty soil. What shall I do now?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Thish old shervant is afraid and he won't look into the cart. Will you look into the cart, shir?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ I see no harm in that. Yes, I will do it.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Are those things jackals that I shee flying into the air, and are those things crows that walk on all fours? While the witch is chewing him with her eyes, and looking at him with her teeth, I 'll make my eshcape.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Perceives Vasantasena. Sadly to himself._] Is it possible? The gazelle follows the tiger. Alas!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Her mate is lovely as the autumn moon, Who waits for her upon the sandy dune; And yet the swan will leave him? and will go To dance attendance on a common crow? 16
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Aside to Vasantasena._] Ah, Vasantasena! This is neither right, nor worthy of you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Your pride rejected him before, Yet now for gold, and for your mother's will
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ No! [_She shakes her head._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Your nature knows your pride no more; You honor him, a common woman still. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Did I not tell you to "serve the man you love, and him you hate"?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ I made a mistake in the cart, and thus I came hither. I throw myself upon your protection.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Do not fear. Come, I must deceive him. [_He returns to Sansthanaka._] Jackass, there is indeed a witch who makes her home in the cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ But shir, if a witch is living there, why are n't you robbed? And if it 's a thief, why are n't you eaten alive?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Why try to determine that? But if we should go back on foot through the gardens until we came to the city, to Ujjayini, what harm would that do?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ And if we did, what then?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Then we should have some exercise, and should avoid tiring the bullocks.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ All right. Sthavaraka, my shlave, drive on. But no! Shtop, shtop! I go on foot before gods and Brahmans? Not much! I 'll go in my cart, sho that people shall shee me a long way off, and shay "There he goes, our mashter, the king's brother-in-law."
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Aside._] It is hard to convert poison into medicine. So be it, then. [_Aloud._] Jackass, this is Vasantasena, come to visit you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Heaven forbid!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Gleefully._] Oh, oh! To visit me, an arishtocrat, a man, a regular Vasudeva?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Yes.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ This is an unheard-of piece of luck. That other time I made her angry, sho now I 'll fall at her feet and beg her pardon.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Capital!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I 'll fall at her feet myshelf. [_He approaches Vasantasena._] Little mother, mamma dear, lishten to my prayer.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: I fold my hands and fall before thy feet-- Thine eyes are large, thy teeth are clean and neat, Thy finger-nails are ten--forgive thy shlave What, love-tormented, he offended, shweet. 18
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Angrily._] Leave me! Your words are an insult! [_She spurns him with her foot._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Wrathfully._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Thish head that mother and that mamma kissed, That never bent to worship god, I wist, Upon thish head she dared to plant her feet, Like jackals on the carrion they meet. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Sthavaraka, you shlave, where did you pick her up?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Master, the highway was blocked by villagers' wagons. So I stopped my cart near Charudatta's orchard, and got out. And while I was helping a villager with his wagon, I suppose she mistook this cart for another, and climbed in.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Oho! she mishtook my cart for another? and did n't come to shee me? Get out of my cart, get out! You 're going to visit your poor merchant's shon, are you? Those are my bullocks you 're driving. Get out, get out, you shlave! Get out, get out!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Truly, you honor me when you say that I came to see Charudatta. Now what must be, must be.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: These hands of mine, ten-finger-naily, These hands sho lotush-leafy, Are itching-anxious, girl, to dally With you; and in a jiffy I 'll drag Your Shweetness by the hair From the cart wherein you ride, As did Jatayu Bali's fair, The monkey Bali's bride. 20
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: So virtuous ladies may not be Insulted thus despitefully; Nor garden creepers may not be Robbed of their leaves so cruelly. 21
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Stand up, man. I will help her to alight. Come, Vasantasena! [_Vasantasena alights and stands apart._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Aside._] The flame of wrath was kindled when she despised my proposition, and now it blazes up because she kicked me. Sho now I 'll murder her. Good! Thish way. [_Aloud._] Well, shir, what do you want?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: A cloak with fringes hanging down and all, Tied with a hundred shtrings? or good ragout, To make you shmack your greedy lips and call "Chuhoo, chuhoo, chukku, chuhoo, chuhooo"? 22
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Well?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Do me a favor.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Certainly. Anything, unless it be a sin.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ There's not a shmell of a shin in it, shir. Not a perfume!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Speak, then.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Murder Vasantasena.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Stopping his ears._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: A tender lady, gem of this our city, A courtezan whose love was stainless ever-- If I should kill her, sinless, without pity. What boat would bear me on the gloomy river? 23
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I'll give you a boat. And beshides, in thish deserted garden, who'll shee you murdering her?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The regions ten, the forest gods, the sky, The wind, the moon, the sun whose rays are light, Virtue, my conscience--these I cannot fly, Nor earth, that witnesses to wrong and right. 24
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Well then, put your cloak over her and murder her.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ You fool! You scoundrel!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ The old hog is afraid of a shin. Never mind. I'll pershuade Sthavaraka, my shlave. Sthavaraka, my little shon, my shlave, I'll give you golden bracelets.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ And I'll wear them.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I'll have a golden sheat made for you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ And I'll sit on it.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I'll give you all my leavings.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ And I'll eat them.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I'll make you the chief of all my shervants.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Master, I'll be the chief.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ You only have to attend to what I shay.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Master, I will do anything, unless it be a sin.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ There's not a shmell of a shin in it.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Then speak, master.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Murder Vasantasena.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Oh, master, be merciful! Unworthy as I am, I brought this worthy lady hither, because she mistook this bullock-cart for another.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ You shlave, ain't I your mashter?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Master of my body, not of my character. Be merciful, master, be merciful! I am afraid.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ You're my shlave. Who are you afraid of?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Of the other world, master.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Who is thish "other world"?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Master, it is a rewarder of righteousness and sin.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ What is the reward of righteoushness?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ To be like my master, with plenty of golden ornaments.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ What is the reward of shin?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ To be like me, eating another man's bread. That is why I will do no sin.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Sho you won't murder her? [_He beats him with all his might._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ You may beat me, master. You may kill me, master. I will do no sin.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: A luckless, lifelong slave am I, A slave I live, a slave I die; But further woe I will not buy, I will not, will not sin. 25
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Sir, I throw myself upon your protection.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Pardon him, jackass! Well done, Sthavaraka!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Does this poor, miserable slave Seek virtue's meed beyond the grave? And is his lord indifferent? Then why are not such creatures sent To instant hell, whose sinful store Grows great, who know not virtue more? 26
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Ah, cruel, cruel is our fate, And enters through the straitest gate; Since he is slave, and you are lord, Since he does not enjoy your hoard, Since you do not obey his word. 27
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Aside._] The old jackal is afraid of a shin, and the "lifelong shlave" is afraid of the other world. Who am I afraid of, I, the king's brother-in-law, an arishtocrat, a man? [_Aloud._] Well, shervant, you "lifelong shlave," you can go. Go to your room and resht and keep out of my way.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Yes, master. [_To Vasantasena._] Madam, I have no further power. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Girds up his loins._] Wait a minute, Vasantasena, wait a minute. I want to murder you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ You will kill her before my eyes? [_He seizes him by the throat._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Falls to the ground._] Shir, you 're murdering your mashter. [_He loses consciousness, but recovers._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: I always fed him fat with meat, And gave him butter too, to eat; Now for the friend in need I search; Why does he leave me in the lurch? 28
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_After reflection._] Good! I have an idea. The old jackal gave her a hint by shaking his head at her. Sho I 'll shend him away, and then I 'll murder Vasantasena. That's the idea. [_Aloud._] Shir, I was born in a noble family as great as a wine-glass. How could I do that shin I shpoke about? I jusht shaid it to make her love me.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Why should you boast of this your noble birth?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: 'T is character that makes the man of worth; But thorns and weeds grow rank in fertile earth. 29
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ She 's ashamed to confessh her love when you 're here. Please go. My shervant Sthavaraka has gone too after getting a beating. He may be running away. Catch him, shir, and come back with him.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Vasantasena is too proud to own. While I am near, her love for one so crude; So now I leave her here with him alone; Love's confidences long for solitude. 30
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Aloud._] Very well. I go.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Seizing the hem of his garment._] Did I not throw myself upon your protection?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Do not fear, Vasantasena. Jackass, Vasantasena is a pledge, committed to your hand.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ All right. Jusht let her be committed to my hand. It 's a pledge that I 'll execute.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Are you honest?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Honesht.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Takes a few steps._] No! If I go, the wretch might kill her. I will conceal myself for a moment, and see what he intends to do. [_He stands apart._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Good! I 'll murder her. But no! Perhaps thish tricky trickshter, thish Brahman, thish old jackal, has gone and hidden himshelf; he might raise a howl like the jackal he is. I 'll jusht do thish to deceive him. [_He gathers flowers and adorns himself._] Vasantasena, my love, my love! Come!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Yes, he has turned lover. Good! I am content. I will go. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: I 'll give you gold, I 'll call you shweet; My turbaned head adores your feet. Why not love me, my clean-toothed girl? Why worship such a pauper churl? 31
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ How can you ask? [_She bows her head and recites the following verses._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: O base and vile! O wretch! What more? Why tempt me now with gold and power? The honey-loving bees adore The pure and stainless lotus flower. 32
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Though poverty may strike a good man low, Peculiar honor waits upon his woe; And 't is the glory of a courtezan To set her love upon an honest man. 33
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: And I, who have loved the mango-tree, I cannot cling to the locust-tree.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Wench, you make that poor little Charudatta into a mango-tree, and me you call a locusht-tree, not even an acacia! That 's the way you abuse me, and even yet you remember Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Why should I not remember him who dwells in my heart?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Thish very minute I 'm going to shtrangle "him who dwells in your heart," and you too. Shtand shtill, you poor-merchant-man's lover!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Oh speak, oh speak again these words that do me honor!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Jusht let poor Charudatta--the shon of a shlave--reshcue you now!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ He would rescue me, if he saw me.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Is he the king of gods? the royal ape? Shon of a nymph? or wears a demon's shape? The kingly deity of wind and rain? The offshpring of the Pandu-princes' bane? A prophet? or a vulture known afar? A shtatesman? or a beetle? or a shtar? 34
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: But even if he was, he could n't reshcue you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: As Sita in the Bharata Was killed by good old Chanakya, Sho I intend to throttle thee, As did Jatayu Draupadi. 35
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_He raises his arm to strike her._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Mother! where are you? Oh, Charudatta! my heart's longing is unfulfilled, and now I die! I will scream for help. No! It would bring shame on Vasantasena, should she scream for help. Heaven bless Charudatta!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Does the wench shpeak that rashcal's name even yet? [_He seizes her by the throat._] Remember him, wench, remember him!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Heaven bless Charudatta!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Die, wench! [_He strangles her. Vasantasena loses consciousness, and falls motionless._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Gleefully._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Thish bashketful of shin, thish wench, Thish foul abode of impudence-- She came to love, she shtayed to blench, For Death's embrace took every sense. But why boasht I of valorous arms and shtout? She shimply died because her breath gave out. Like Sita in the Bharata, she lies. Ah, mother mine! how prettily she dies. 36
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: She would not love me, though I loved the wench; I shaw the empty garden, set the shnare, And frightened her, and made the poor girl blench. My brother! Oh, my father! Thish is where You misshed the shight of heroism shtout; Your brother and your shon here blosshomed out Into a man; like Mother Draupadi, You were not there, my bravery to shee. 37
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Good! The old jackal will be here in a minute. I 'll shtep ashide and wait. [_He does so._] [_Enter the courtier, with Sthavaraka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ I have persuaded the servant Sthavaraka to come back, and now I will look for the jackass. [_He walks about and looks around him._] But see! A tree has fallen by the roadside, and killed a woman in its fall. O cruel! How couldst thou do this deed of shame? And when I see that a woman was slain by thy fatal fall, I too am felled to the earth. Truly, my heart's fear for Vasantasena was an evil omen. Oh, heaven grant that all may yet be well! [_He approaches Sansthanaka._] Jackass, I have persuaded your servant Sthavaraka to return.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ How do you do, shir? Sthavaraka, my little shon, my shlave, how do you do?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Well, thank you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Give me my pledge.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ What pledge?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Vasantasena.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ She's gone.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Where?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Right after you.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Doubtfully._] No, she did not go in that direction.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ In what direction did you go?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Toward the east.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Well, she went shouth.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ So did I.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ She went north.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ This is nonsense. My heart is not satisfied. Speak the truth.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ I shwear by your head, shir, and my own feet. You may be easy in your heart. I murdered her.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Despairingly._] You really killed her?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ If you don't believe my words, then shee the firsht heroic deed of Sansthanaka, the king's brother-in-law. [_He points out the body._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Alas! Ah, woe is me! [_He falls in a swoon._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Hee, hee! The gentleman is calm enough now!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Oh, sir! Come to yourself! I am the first murderer, for I brought the bullock-cart hither without looking into it.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Comes to himself. Mournfully._] Alas, Vasantasena!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The stream of courtesy is dried away, And happiness to her own land doth flee, Sweet gem of gems, that knew love's gentle play, Love's mart and beauty's! Joy of men like me! Thy mirth-shored stream, that kind and healing river-- Alas! is perished, lost, and gone forever! 38
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Tearfully._] Ah, woe is me!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: What sin is yet to come, or woe, Now thou hast done this deed of hate? Like sin's foul self, hast thou laid low The sinless goddess of our state. 39
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Aside._] Ah! Perhaps the wretch means to lay this sin to my charge. I must go hence. [_He walks about. Sansthanaka approaches and holds him back._] Scoundrel! Touch me not. I have done with you. I go.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Aha! Firsht you murder Vasantasena, then you abuse me, and now where will you run to? And sho a man like me has n't anybody to protect him.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ You are an accursèd scoundrel!
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: I'll give you countless wealth, a piece of gold, A copper, and a cap, to have and hold. And sho the fame of thish great deed shall be A common property, and shan't touch me. 40
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ A curse upon you! Yours, and yours only, be the deed.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Heaven avert the omen! [_Sansthanaka bursts out laughing._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Be enmity between us! Cease your mirth! Damned be a friendship that so shames my worth! Never may I set eyes on one so low! I fling you off, an unstrung, broken bow. 41
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Don't be angry. Come, let's go and play in the pond.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Unstained my life, and yet it seems to me Your friendship stains, and mocks my sinlessness, You woman-murderer! How could I be A friend to one whom women ever see With eyes half-closed in apprehension's stress? 42
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Mournfully._] Vasantasena,
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA
