text: When thou, sweet maid, art born again, Be not a courtezan reborn, But in a house which sinless men, And virtuous, and good, adorn. 43
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Firsht you murder Vasantasena in my old garden Pushpakaranda, and now where will you run to? Come, defend yourshelf in court before my shishter's husband! [_He holds him back._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ Enough, you accursèd scoundrel! [_He draws his sword._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Recoiling in terror._] Shcared, are you? Go along, then.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Courtier._ [_Aside._] It would be folly to remain here. Well, I will go and join myself to Sharvilaka, Chandanaka, and the rest. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Go to hell. Well, my little shon Sthavaraka, what kind of a thing is thish that I 've done?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Master, you have committed a terrible crime.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Shlave! What do you mean by talking about a crime? Well, I 'll do it thish way. [_He takes various ornaments from his person._] Take these gems. I give 'em to you. Whenever I want to wear them, I 'll take them back again, but the resht of the time they are yours.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ They should be worn only by my master. What have I to do with such things?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ Go along! Take these bullocks, and wait in the tower of my palace until I come.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sthavaraka._ Yes, master. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Sansthanaka._ The gentleman has made himshelf invisible. He wanted to save himshelf. And the shlave I 'll put in irons in the palace tower, and keep him there. And sho the shecret will be shafe. I 'll go along, but firsht I 'll take a look at her. Is she dead, or shall I murder her again? [_He looks at Vasantasena._] Dead as a doornail! Good! I 'll cover her with thish cloak. No, it has my name on it. Shome honesht man might recognize it. Well, here are shome dry leaves that the wind has blown into a heap. I 'll cover her with them. [_He does so, then pauses to reflect._] Good! I 'll do it thish way. I 'll go to court at once, and there I 'll lodge a complaint. I 'll shay that the merchant Charudatta enticed Vasantasena into my old garden Pushpakaranda, and killed her for her money.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Yesh, Charudatta musht be shlaughtered now, And I 'll invent the plan, forgetting pity; The shacrificing of a sinless cow Is cruel in the kindesht-hearted city. 44
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Now I 'm ready to go. [_He starts to go away, but perceives something that frightens him._] Goodnessh gracioush me! Wherever I go, thish damned monk comes with his yellow robes. I bored a hole in his nose once and drove him around, and he hates me. Perhaps he'll shee me, and will tell people that I murdered her. How shall I eshcape? [_He looks about._] Aha! I 'll jump over the wall where it is half fallen down, and eshcape that way.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: I run, I run, I go, In heaven, on earth below, In hell, and in Ceylon, Hanumat's peaks upon-- Like Indra's self, I go. [_Exit._] 45
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Enter hurriedly the Buddhist monk, ex-shampooer._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ I 've washed these rags of mine. Shall I let them dry on a branch? no, the monkeys would steal them. On the ground? the dust would make them dirty again. Well then, where shall I spread them out to dry? [_He looks about._] Ah, here is a pile of dry leaves which the wind has blown into a heap. I 'll spread them out on that. [_He does so._] Buddha be praised! [_He sits down._] Now I will repeat a hymn of the faith.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: Who slays the Five Men, and the Female Bane, By whom protection to the Town is given, By whom the Outcaste impotent is slain, He cannot fail to enter into heaven. (2)
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: After all, what have I to do with heaven, before I have paid my debt to Vasantasena, my sister in Buddha? She bought my freedom for ten gold-pieces from the gamblers, and since that day I regard myself as her property. [_He looks about._] What was that? a sigh that arose from the leaves? It cannot be.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The heated breezes heat the leaves, The wetted garment wets the leaves, And so, I guess, the scattered leaves Curl up like any other leaves. 46
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Vasantasena begins to recover consciousness, and stretches out her hand._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ Ah, there appears a woman's hand, adorned with beautiful gems. What! a second hand? [_He examines it with the greatest care._] It seems to me, I recognize this hand. Yes, there is no doubt about it. Surely, this is the hand that saved me. But I must see for myself. [_He uncovers the body, looks at it, and recognizes it._] It _is_ my sister in Buddha. [_Vasantasena pants for water._] Ah, she seeks water, and the pond is far away. What shall I do? An idea! I will hold this robe over her and let it drip upon her. [_He does so. Vasantasena recovers consciousness, and raises herself. The monk fans her with his garment._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ Who are you, sir?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ Has my sister in Buddha forgotten him whose freedom she bought for ten gold-pieces?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ I seem to remember, but not just as you say. It were better that I had slept never to waken.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ What happened here, sister in Buddha?
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Vasantasena._ [_Despairingly._] Nothing but what is fitting--for a courtezan.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ Sister in Buddha, support yourself by this creeper that clings to the tree, and rise to your feet [_He bends down the creeper. Vasantasena takes it in her hand, and rises._]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: _Monk._ In yonder monastery dwells one who is my sister in the faith. There shall my sister in Buddha be restored before she returns home. You must walk very slowly, sister. [_He walks about and looks around him._] Make way, good people, make way! This is a young lady, and I am a monk, yet my conduct is above reproach.
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: The man whose hands, whose lips are free from greed, Who curbs his senses, he is man indeed. He little recks, if kingdoms fall or stand; For heaven is in the hollow of his hand. 47
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [Footnote 73: The five senses.]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [Footnote 74: Ignorance.]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [Footnote 75: The body.]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [Footnote 76: The conceit of individuality.]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [Footnote 77: Used as an appetiser.]
chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

chapter_title: ACT THE EIGHTH: THE STRANGLING OF VASANTASENA

text: [_Enter a beadle._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The magistrates said to me "Come, beadle, go to the court-room, and make ready the seats." So now I am on my way to set the court-room in order. [_He walks about and looks around him._] Here is the court-room, I will enter. [_He enters, sweeps, and puts a seat in its place._] There! I have tidied up the court-room and put the seats in readiness, and now I will go and tell the magistrates. [_He walks about and looks around him._] But see! Here comes that arrant knave, the king's brother-in-law. I will go away without attracting his attention. [_He stands apart. Enter Sansthanaka, in gorgeous raiment._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: I bathed where water runs and flows and purls; I shat within a garden, park, and grove With women, and with females, and with girls, Whose lovely limbs with grace angelic move. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My hair is shometimes done up tight, you shee; In locks, or curls, it hangs my forehead o'er; Shometimes 't is matted, shometimes hanging free; And then again, I wear a pompadour. I am a wonder, I'm a wondrous thing. And the husband of my shishter is the king. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: And beshides, I 've found a big hole, like a worm that has crawled into the knot of a lotush-root, and is looking for a hole to creep out at. Now who was I going to accuse of thish wicked deed? [_He recalls something._] Oh, yesh! I remember. I was going to accuse poor Charudatta of thish wicked deed. Beshides, he's poor. They 'll believe anything about him. Good! I 'll go to the court-room and lodge a public complaint against Charudatta, how he shtrangled Vasantasena and murdered her. Sho now I 'm on my way to the court-room. [_He walks about and looks around him._] Here is the court-room. I 'll go in. [_He enters and looks about._] Well, here are the sheats, all arranged. While I 'm waiting for the magishtrates, I 'll jusht sit down a minute on the grass. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ [_Walks about in another direction, and looks before him._] Here come the magistrates. I will go to them. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Enter the judge, accompanied by a gild-warden, a clerk, and others._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Gild-warden and clerk!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ We await your bidding.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ A trial depends to such an extent upon others that the task of the magistrates--the reading of another's thoughts--is most difficult.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Men often speak of deeds that no man saw, Matters beyond the province of the law; Passion so rules the parties that their lies, Hide their offenses from judicial eyes; This side and that exaggerate a thing, Until at last it implicates the king; To sum it up: false blame is easy won, A true judge little praised, or praised by none. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Men often point to sins that no man saw, And in their anger scorn the patient law; In court-rooms even the righteous with their lies Hide their offenses from judicial eyes; And those who did the deed are lost to view, Who sinned with plaintiff and defendant too; To sum it up: false blame is easy won, A true judge little praised, or praised by none. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: For the judge must be
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Learnèd, and skilled in tracing fraud's sly path, And eloquent, insensible to wrath; To friend, foe, kinsman showing equal grace, Reserving judgment till he know the case; Untouched by avarice, in virtue sound. The weak he must defend, the knave confound; An open door to truth, his heart must cling To others' interests, yet shun each thing That might awake the anger of the king. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ And do men speak of defects in your virtue? If so, then they speak of darkness in the moonlight.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good beadle, conduct me to the court-room.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Follow me, Your Honor. [_They walk about._] Here is the court-room. May the magistrates be pleased to enter. [_All enter._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good beadle, do you go outside and learn who desires to present a case.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Yes, sir. [_He goes out._] Gentlemen, the magistrates ask if there is any here who desires to present a case.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Gleefully._] The magishtrates are here. [_He struts about._] I desire to present a cashe, I, an arishtocrat, a man, a Vasudeva, the royal brother-in-law, the brother-in-law of the king.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ [_In alarm._] Goodness! The king's brother-in-law is the first who desires to present a case. Well! Wait a moment, sir. I will inform the magistrates at once. [_He approaches the magistrates._] Gentlemen, here is the king's brother-in-law who has come to court, desiring to present a case.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ What! the king's brother-in-law is the first who desires to present a case? Like an eclipse at sunrise, this betokens the ruin of some great man. Beadle, the court will doubtless be very busy to-day. Go forth, my good man, and say "Leave us for to-day. Your suit cannot be considered."
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Yes, Your Honor. [_He goes out, and approaches Sansthanaka._] Sir, the magistrates send word that you are to leave them for to-day; that your suit cannot be considered.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Wrathfully._] Confound it! Why can't my shuit be conshidered? If it is n't conshidered, then I 'll tell my brother-in-law, King Palaka, my shishter's husband, and I 'll tell my shishter and my mother too, and I 'll have thish judge removed, and another judge appointed. [_He starts to go away._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Oh, sir! Brother-in-law of the king! Wait a moment. I will inform the magistrates at once. [_He returns to the Judge._] The brother-in-law of the king is angry, and says--[_He repeats Sansthanaka's words._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ This fool might do anything. My good man, tell him to come hither, that his suit will be considered.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ [_Approaching Sansthanaka._] Sir, the magistrates send word that you are to come in, that your suit will be considered. Pray enter, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Firsht they shay it won't be conshidered, then they shay it will be conshidered. The magishtrates are shcared. Whatever I shay, I 'll make 'em believe it. Good! I 'll enter. [_He enters and approaches the magistrates._] I am feeling very well, thank you. Whether you feel well or not--that depends on me.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ [_Aside._] Well, well! We seem to have a highly cultivated plaintiff. [_Aloud._] Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Well! Thish floor belongs to me. I 'll sit down wherever I like. [_To the gild-warden._] I'll sit here. [_To the beadle._] Why should n't I sit here? [_He lays his hand on the Judge's head._] I 'll sit here. [_He sits down on the floor._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ You desire to present a case?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Of courshe.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Then state the case.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ I 'll whishper it. I was born in the great family of a man as glorioush as a wine-glass.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My father's father of the king--in law; The king, he is my daddy's son-in-law; And I am brother to the king--in law; And the husband of my shishter is the king. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ All this we know.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Why should you boast of this your noble birth? 'T is character that makes the man of worth; But thorns and weeds grow rank in fertile earth. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: State your case.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ I will, but even if I was guilty, he wouldn't do anything to me. Well, my shishter's husband liked me, and gave me the besht garden there is, the old garden Pushpakaranda, to play in and look after. And there I go every day to look at it, to keep it dry, to keep it clean, to keep it blosshoming, to keep it trimmed. But fate decreed that I shaw--or rather, I didn't _shee_--the proshtrate body of a woman.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Do you know who the unfortunate woman was?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Hello, magishtrates! Why shouldn't I know? A woman like that! the pearl of the city! adorned with a hundred golden ornaments! Shomebody's unworthy shon enticed her into the old garden Pushpakaranda when it was empty, and for a mere trifle--for her money!--shtrangled Vasantasena and killed her. But _I_ didn't--[_He breaks off, and puts his hand over his mouth._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ What carelessness on the part of the city police! Gild-warden and clerk, write down the words "I didn't," as the first article in the case.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Clerk._ Yes, sir. [_He does so._] Sir, it is written.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Aside._] Goodnessh! Now I've ruined myshelf, like a man that shwallows a cake of rice and milk in a hurry. Well, I'll get out of it thish way. [_Aloud._] Well, well, magishtrates! I was jusht remarking that I didn't shee it happen. What are you making thish hullabaloo about? [_He wipes out the written words with his foot._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ How do you know that she was strangled--and for her money?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Hello! Why shouldn't I think sho, when her neck was shwollen and bare, and the places where you wear jewels did n't have any gold on them?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ That seems plausible.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Aside._] Thank heaven! I breathe again. Hooray!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Upon whom does the conduct of this case depend?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ The case has a twofold aspect.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ How so?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ We have to consider the allegations, then the facts. Now the investigation of the allegations depends upon plaintiff and defendant. But the investigation of the facts must be carried out by the wisdom of the judge.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Then the conduct of the case depends upon the presence of Vasantasena's mother?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Precisely. My good beadle, summon Vasantasena's mother, without, however, giving her cause for anxiety.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Yes, Your Honor. [_He goes out, and returns with the mother of the courtezan._] Follow me, madam.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ My daughter went to the house of a friend to enjoy her youth. But now comes this gentleman--long life to him!--and says "Come! The judge summons you." I find myself quite bewildered. My heart is palpitating. Sir, will you conduct me to the court-room?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Follow me, madam. [_They walk about._] Here is the court-room. Pray enter, madam. [_They enter._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ [_Approaching._] Happiness be yours, most worthy gentlemen.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good woman, you are very welcome. Pray be seated.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ Thank you. [_She seats herself._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Abusively._] You 're here, are you, you old bawd?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Tell me. Are you Vasantasena's mother?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ I am.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Whither has Vasantasena gone at this moment?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ To the house of a friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ What is the name of her friend?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ [_Aside._] Dear me! Really, this is very embarrassing. [_Aloud._] Any one else might ask me this, but not a judge.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Pray do not be embarrassed. The conduct of the case puts the question.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ The conduct of the case puts the question. You incur no fault. Speak.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ What! the conduct of the case? If that is so, then listen, worthy gentlemen. There lives in the merchants' quarter the grandson of the merchant Vinayadatta, the son of Sagaradatta, a man whose name is a good omen in itself--that name is Charudatta. In his house my daughter enjoys her youth.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Did you hear that? Write those words down. My contention is with Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ It is no sin for Charudatta to be her friend.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ The conduct of this case demands the presence of Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Exactly.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Dhanadatta, write as the first article in the case "Vasantasena went to the house of Charudatta." But must we summon the worthy Charudatta also? No, the conduct of the case summons him. Go, my good beadle, summon Charudatta,--but gently, without haste, without giving him cause for anxiety, respectfully, as it were incidentally,--with the words "The judge wishes to see you."
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Yes, Your Honor. [_He goes out, then returns with Charudatta._] Follow me, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Thoughtfully._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My character and kin are known Unto the king who rules our state; And in this summons there is shown A doubt begotten of my wretched fate. 8
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Reflectively. Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Ah! Were there those, the man to recognize Who met me on the road, from bondage freed? Or did the king, who sees through cunning spies, Learn that my cart was lent him in his need? Why should I else be forced to tread the street, Like one accused of crime, my judge to meet? 9
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: But why consider thus? I must go to the court-room. My good beadle, conduct me to the court.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Follow me, sir. [_They walk about._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Apprehensively._] And what means this?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Hear how the gloomy raven hoarsely croaks; The slaves of justice summon me again; My left eye twitches; these repeated strokes Of threatened evil frighten me and pain. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Follow me, sir, gently and without haste.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Walks about and looks before him._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Upon the withered tree, a crow Turns to the sun; His left eye falls on me. Ah, woe! My doubt is done. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_He looks in another direction._] But see! a snake!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: His eye is fixed upon me; and his back Flashes like antimony's lustrous black; His long tongue quivers; four white fangs appear; His belly swells and coils. He slumbered here, This prince of serpents, till I crossed his path, And now he darts upon me in his wrath. 12
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: And more than this:
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: I slip, although the ground has felt no rain; My left eye, and my left arm throb again; Another bird is screaming overhead; All bodes a cruel death, and hope is fled. 13
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Surely, the gods will grant that all may yet be well.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Follow me, sir. Here is the court-room. Pray enter.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Enters and looks about._] How wonderfully splendid is the court-room. For it seems an ocean,
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Whose waters are the king's advisers, deep In thought; as waves and shells it seems to keep The attorneys; and as sharks and crocodiles It has its spies that stand in waiting files; Its elephants and horses represent The cruel ocean-fish on murder bent; As if with herons of the sea, it shines With screaming pettifoggers' numerous lines; While in the guise of serpents, scribes are creeping Upon its statecraft-trodden shore: the court The likeness of an ocean still is keeping, To which all harmful-cruel beasts resort. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Come! [_As he enters, he strikes his head against the door. Reflectively._] Alas! This also?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My left eye throbs; a raven cries; A serpent coils athwart my path. My safety now with heaven lies. 15
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: But I must enter. [_He does so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ This is Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: A countenance like his, with clear-cut nose, Whose great, wide-opened eye frank candor shows, Is not the home of wantonness; With elephants, with horses, and with kine, The outer form is inner habit's sign; With men no less. 16
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ My greetings to the officers of justice. Officials, I salute you.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ [_Betraying his agitation._] You are very welcome, sir. My good beadle, give the gentleman a seat.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ [_Brings a seat._] Here is a seat. Pray be seated, sir. [_Charudatta seats himself._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Angrily._] You're here, are you, you woman-murderer? Well! Thish is a fine trial, thish is a jusht trial, where they give a sheat to thish woman-murderer. [_Haughtily._] But it's all right. They can give it to him.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Charudatta, have you any attachment, or affection, or friendship, with this lady's daughter?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ What lady?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ This lady. [_He indicates Vasantasena's mother._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Rising._] Madam, I salute you.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ Long life to you, my son! [_Aside._] So this is Charudatta. My daughter's youth is in good hands.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Sir, is the courtezan your friend? [_Charudatta betrays his embarrassment._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: He tries to hide the deed he did; He lies, from shame or fear; He murdered her, of her got rid For gold, and thinks the deed is hid; Not sho his mashter here. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Speak, Charudatta. Do not be ashamed. This is a lawsuit.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_In embarrassment._] Officials, how can I testify that a courtezan is my friend? But at worst, it is youth that bears the blame, not character.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The case is hard; then banish shame, Though it oppress your heart; Speak truth with fortitude, and aim To set deceit apart. 18
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Do not be embarrassed. The conduct of the case puts the question.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Officer, with whom have I a lawsuit?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Arrogantly._] With me!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ A lawsuit with you is unendurable!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Well, well, woman-murderer! You murder a woman like Vasantasena who used to wear a hundred gems, and now you try deceitful deceivings to hide it!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ You are a fool.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Enough of him, good Charudatta. Speak the truth. Is the courtezan your friend?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ She is.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Sir, where is Vasantasena?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ She has gone home.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ How did she go? When did she go? Who accompanied her?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Aside._] Shall I say that she went unobserved?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Speak, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ She went home. What more shall I say?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ She was enticed into my old garden Pushpakaranda, and was shtrangled for her money. Now will you shay that she went home?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Man, you are crazy.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The very clouds of heaven wet not you; Your lips are like the blue-jay's wing-tip worn, Yes, full as fickle with their speech untrue, And like the winter lotus lustre-lorn. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ [_Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Take the Himalayan hills within your hand, And swim from ocean strand to ocean strand, And hold within your grasp the fleeting wind: Then may you think that Charudatta sinned. 20
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Aloud._] This is the noble Charudatta. How could he commit this crime? [_He repeats the verse_ "A countenance like his:" _page 141._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Why thish partiality in a lawshuit?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Away, you fool!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Illiterate, you gloss the Sacred Law, And still your tongue uninjured find? The midday sun with steadfast eye you saw, And are not straightway stricken blind? You thrust your hand into the blazing fire, And draw it forth, unscathed and sound? Drag Charudatta's virtue in the mire, Nor sink beneath this yawning ground? 21
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: How could the noble Charudatta commit a crime?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Of all the riches of the mighty sea Only the swelling waters now are left, Because, without consideration, he-- For others' good--himself of all has reft. And should this high-souled man, this store-house where All gems of virtue gather and unite, For lucre's sake, so foul a trespass dare That in it even his foe could not delight? 22
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ You scoundrel! When the golden casket that was left with him as a pledge was stolen by thieves at night, he gave in place of it a pearl necklace that was the pride of the four seas. And he should now, for a mere trifle--for her money!--do this sin? Oh, my child, come back to me, my daughter! [_She weeps._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Noble Charudatta, did she go on foot, or in a bullock-cart?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ I did not see her when she went. Therefore I do not know whether she went on foot, or in a bullock-cart.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Enter Viraka, in anger._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My anger was so prodded to the quick, By that dishonoring, insulting kick, And so I brooded, till at last the night Unwilling yielded to the dawning light. 23
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: So now I will go to the court-room. [_He enters._] May happiness be the lot of these honorable gentlemen.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Ah, it is Viraka, the captain of the guard. Viraka, what is the purpose of your coming?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Viraka._ Well! I was looking for Aryaka, in all the excitement about his escape from prison. I had my suspicions about a covered bullock-cart that was coming, and wanted to look in. "You 've made one inspection, man, I must make another," said I, and then I was kicked by the highly respectable Chandanaka. You have heard the matter, gentlemen. The rest is your affair.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good man, do you know to whom the bullock-cart belonged?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Viraka._ To this gentleman here, Charudatta. And the driver said that Vasantasena was in it, and was on her way to have a good time in the old garden Pushpakaranda.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Lishten to that, too!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: This moon, alas, though spotless-bright, Is now eclipsed, and robbed of light; The bank is fallen; the waves appear Befouled, that once were bright and clear. 24
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Viraka, we will investigate your case here later. Mount the horse that stands before the court-room door, go to the garden Pushpakaranda, and see whether a woman has perished there or not.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Viraka._ Yes, sir. [_He goes out, then returns._] I have been there. And I saw the body of a woman, torn by wild beasts.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ How do you know that it was the body of a woman?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Viraka._ That I perceived from the traces of hair and arms and hands and feet.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Alas for the difficulties which are caused by the actions of men!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The more one may apply his skill, The harder is the matter still; Plain are indeed the law's demands, Yet judgment insecurely stands As some poor cow on shifting sands. 25
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: As bees, when flowers begin to blow, Gather to sip the honey, so When man is marked by adverse fate, Misfortunes enter every gate. 26
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Noble Charudatta, speak truth!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: A mean and jealous creature, passion-blind, Sets all his soul, some fatal means to find To slay the man he envies; shall his lies By evil nature prompted, win the prize? No! he is unregarded by the wise. 27
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: And more than this:
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The creeper's beauty would I never blight, Nor pluck its flowers; should I not be afraid To seize her hair so lovely-long, and bright As wings of bees, and slay a weeping maid? 28
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Hello, magishtrates! How can you inveshtigate the cashe with such partiality? Why, even now you let thish shcoundrel Charudatta shtay on his sheat.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good beadle, so be it [_The beadle follows Sansthanaka's suggestion._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Consider, magistrates, consider what you are doing! [_He leaves his seat, and sits on the floor._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Dancing about gleefully. Aside._] Fine! The shin that I did falls on another man's head. Sho I 'll sit where Charudatta was. [_He does so._] Look at me, Charudatta, and confessh that you murdered her.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Magistrates!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: A mean and jealous creature, passion-blind, Sets all his soul, some fatal means to find To slay the man he envies; shall his lies, By evil nature prompted, win the prize? No! he is unregarded by the wise. (27)
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Sighing. Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My friend Maitreya! Oh, this cruel blow! My wife, thou issue of a spotless strain! My Rohasena! Here am I, laid low By sternest fate; and thou, thou dost not know That all thy childish games are played in vain. Thou playest, heedless of another's pain! 29
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: But Maitreya I sent to Vasantasena, that he might bring me tidings of her, and might restore the jewels which she gave my child, to buy him a toy cart. Why then does he linger?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Enter Maitreya with the gems._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ Charudatta bade me go to Vasantasena, to return her jewels, and he said to me: "Maitreya, Vasantasena adorned my dear Rohasena with her own jewels, and sent him thus to his mother. It was fitting that she should give him the jewels, but not that we should receive them. Therefore restore them to her." So now I will go to Vasantasena's house. [_He walks about and looks around, then speaks to a person behind the scenes._] Ah, it is Master Rebhila. Oh, Master Rebhila, why do you seem so exceedingly troubled? [_He listens._] What! do you mean to say that my dear friend Charudatta has been summoned to court? That can hardly be an insignificant matter. [_He reflects._] I will go to Vasantasena's house later, but now I will go to the court-room. [_He walks about and looks around._] Here is the court-room. I will go in at once. [_He enters._] May happiness be the lot of the magistrates. Where is my friend?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Here.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ My friend, I wish you happiness.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ It will be mine.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ And peace.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ That too will be mine.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ My friend, why do you seem so exceedingly troubled? And why were you summoned?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ My friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: A scoundrel I, who bear the blame, Nor seek in heaven to be blest; A maid--or goddess--'t is the same-- But _he_ will say the rest. 30
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ What? what?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Whispers._] That is it.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ Who says that?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Indicating Sansthanaka._] This poor fellow is the instrument that fate uses to accuse me.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ [_Aside to Charudatta._] Why don't you simply say that she went home?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Though I say it, it is not believed, so unfortunate is my condition.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ But gentlemen! He adorned the city of Ujjayini with mansions, cloisters, parks, temples, pools, and fountains, and he should be mad enough to commit such a crime--and for a mere trifle? [_Wrathfully._] You offspring of a loose wench, you brother-in-law of the king, Sansthanaka, you libertine, you slanderer, you buffoon, you gilded monkey, say it before me! This friend of mine does n't even draw a flowering jasmine creeper to himself, to gather the blossoms, for fear that a twig might perhaps be injured. How should he commit a crime like this, which heaven and earth call accursèd? Just wait, you son of a bawd! Wait till I split your head into a hundred pieces with this staff of mine, as crooked as your heart.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Angrily._] Lishten to that, gentlemen! I have a quarrel, or a lawshuit, with Charudatta. What right has a man with a pate that looks like a caret, to shplit my head into a hundred pieces? Not much! You confounded rashcal! [_Maitreya raises his staff and repeats his words. Sansthanaka rises angrily and strikes him. Maitreya strikes back. During the scuffle the jewels fall from Maitreya's girdle._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Picks up the jewels and examines them. Excitedly._] Look, gentlemen, look! These are the poor girl's jewels! [_Pointing to Charudatta._] For a trifle like thish he murdered her, and killed her too. [_The magistrates all bow their heads._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Aside to Maitreya._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: 'T is thus my fate would vent its gall, That at this moment they should fall, These gems--and with them, I. 31
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ But why don't you simply tell the truth?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ My friend,
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The king perceives with blinded eye, Nor on the truth that eye will bend; Though telling all, I cannot fly A wretched and inglorious end. 32
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Alas! Alas!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: With Mars strives Jupiter, and dies; Beside them both there seems to rise A comet-planet in the skies. 33
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ [_Looking at the casket. To Vasantasena's mother._] Madam, pray examine this golden casket attentively, to see whether it be the same or not.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ [_Examining the casket._] It is similar, but not the same.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Oh, you old bawd! You confessh it with your eyes, and deny it with your lips.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ Away, you scoundrel!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Speak carefully. Is it the same or not?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ Sir, the craftsman's skill captivates the eye. But it is not the same.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good woman, do you know these jewels?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ No, I said. No! I don't recognize them; but perhaps they were made by the same craftsman.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Gild-warden, see!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Gems often seem alike in many ways, When the artist's mind on form and beauty plays; For craftsmen imitate what they have seen, And skilful hands remake what once has been. 34
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Do these jewels belong to Charudatta?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Never!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ To whom then?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ To this lady's daughter.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ How did she lose them?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ She lost them. Yes, so much is true.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Gild-warden and Clerk._ Charudatta, speak the truth in this matter. For you must remember,
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Truth brings well-being in its train; Through speaking truth, no evils rise; Truth, precious syllable!--Refrain From hiding truth in lies. 35
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ The jewels, the jewels! I do not know. But I do know that they were taken from my house.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Firsht you take her into the garden and murder her. And now you hide it by tricky trickinessh.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Noble Charudatta, speak the truth!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Merciless lashes wait to smite This moment on thy tender flesh; And we--we can but think it right. 36
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Of sinless sires I boast my birth, And sin in me was never found; Yet if suspicion taints my worth, What boots it though my heart be sound? 37
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Aside._] And yet I know not what to do with life, so I be robbed of Vasantasena. [_Aloud._] Ah, why waste words?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: A scoundrel I, who bear the blame, Nor think of earth, nor heaven blest; That sweetest maid, in passion's flame-- But _he_ will say the rest. 38
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Killed her! Come, you shay it too. "I killed her."
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ You have said it.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ Lishten, my mashters, lishten! He murdered her! No one but him! Doubt is over. Let punishment be inflicted on the body of thish poor Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Beadle, we must do as the king's brother-in-law says. Guardsmen, lay hold on this Charudatta. [_The guardsmen do so._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ Be merciful, good gentlemen, be merciful! [_She repeats what she had said before, beginning_ "When the golden casket:" _page 143._] If my daughter is killed, she is killed. Let him live for me--bless him! And besides, a lawsuit is a matter between plaintiff and defendant. I am the real plaintiff. So let him go free!
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ You shlave, get out of the way! What have you got to shay about him?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Go, madam. Guardsmen, conduct her forth.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Mother._ Oh, my child, my son! [_Exit weeping._
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_Aside._] I 've done shomething worthy of myshelf. Now I 'll go. [_Exit._
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ Noble Charudatta, the decision lies with us, but the rest depends on the king. And yet, beadle, let King Palaka be reminded of this:
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: The Brahman who has sinned, our laws declare, May not be slain, but banished from the realm, And with his wealth entire abroad may fare. 39
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Yes, Your Honor. [_He goes out, then reënters in tears._] Oh, sirs, I was with the king. And King Palaka says: "Inasmuch as he killed Vasantasena for such a trifle, these same jewels shall be hung about his neck, the drum shall be beaten, he shall be conducted to the southern burying-ground, and there impaled." And whoever else shall commit such a crime, shall be punished with the like dreadful doom.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ Oh, how wanton is this act of King Palaka! Nevertheless,
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: Although his counsellors may plunge a king Into injustice' dangers great, Yet he will reap the woe and suffering; And 't is a righteous fate. 40
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL
ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: And more than this:
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: They who pervert the king's true bent, The white crow's part who play, Have slain their thousands innocent, And slay, and slay, and slay. 41
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: My friend Maitreya, go, greet the mother of my son in my name for the last time. And keep my son Rohasena free from harm.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ When the root is cut away, how can the tree be saved?
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ No, not so.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: When man departs to worlds above, In living son yet liveth he; Bestow on Rohasena love No less than that thou gavest me. 42
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ Oh, my friend! I will prove myself your friend by continuing the life that you leave unfinished.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ And let me see Rohasena for a single moment.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Maitreya._ I will. It is but fitting.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Judge._ My good beadle, remove this man. [_The beadle does so._] Who is there? Let the headsmen receive their orders. [_The guardsmen loose their hold on Charudatta, and all of them go out._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Beadle._ Come with me, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: _Charudatta._ [_Mournfully repeats the verse, page 146, beginning_ "My friend Maitreya!" _Then, as if speaking to one not present._]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: If you had proved my conduct by the fire, By water, poison, scales, and thus had known That I deserved that saws should bite my bone, My Brahman's frame, more could I not desire. You trust a foeman, slay me thus? 'T is well. With sons, and sons' sons, now you plunge to hell! 43
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: I come! I come! [_Exeunt omnes._
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [Footnote 83: Elephants were employed as executioners; and, according to Lalladiksita, the horses served the same purpose.]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [Footnote 84: This refers to the fallen jewels.]
chapter_title: ACT THE NINTH: THE TRIAL

text: [_Enter Charudatta, accompanied by two headsmen._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Then think no longer of the pain; In just a second you 'll be slain. We understand the fashions new To fetter you and kill you too. In chopping heads we never fail, Nor when the victim we impale. 1
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Out of the way, gentlemen, out of the way! This is the noble Charudatta.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: The oleander on his brow, In headsmen's hands you see him now; Like a lamp whose oil runs nearly dry, His light fades gently, ere it die. 2
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Gloomily._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: My body wet by tear-drops falling, falling; My limbs polluted by the clinging mud; Flowers from the graveyard torn, my wreath appalling; For ghastly sacrifice hoarse ravens calling, And for the fragrant incense of my blood. 3
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ Out of the way, gentlemen, out of the way!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Why gaze upon the good man so? The ax of death soon lays him low. Yet good men once sought shelter free, Like birds, upon this kindly tree. 4
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Come, Charudatta, come!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Incalculable are the ways of human destiny, that I am come to such a plight!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Red marks of hands in sandal paste O'er all my body have been placed; The man, with meal and powder strewn, Is now to beast of offering grown. 5
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END
ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_He gazes intently before him._] Alas for human differences! [_Mournfully._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: For when they see the fate that I must brave, With tears for death's poor victim freely given, The citizens cry "shame," yet cannot save,-- Can only pray that I attain to heaven. 6
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ Out of the way, gentlemen, out of the way! Why do you gaze upon him?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: God Indra moving through the sky, The calving cow, the falling star, The good man when he needs must die,-- These four behold not from afar. 7
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Goha._ Look, Ahinta! Look, man!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: While he, of citizens the best, Goes to his death at fate's behest, Does heaven thus weep that he must die? Does lightning paint the cloudless sky? 8
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Ahinta._ Goha, man,
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: The heaven weeps not that he must die, Nor lightning paints the cloudless sky; Yet streams are falling constantly From many a woman's clouded eye. 9
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: While this poor victim to his death is led, No man nor woman here but sorely weeps; And so the dust, by countless tear-drops fed, Thus peacefully upon the highway sleeps. 10
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Gazes intently. Mournfully._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: These women, in their palaces who stay, From half-shut windows peering, thus lament, "Alas for Charudatta! Woe the day!" And pity-streaming eyes on me are bent. 11
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ Come, Charudatta, come! Here is the place of proclamation. Beat the drum and proclaim the sentence.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Listen, good people, listen! This is the noble Charudatta, son of Sagaradatta, and grandson of the merchant Vinayadatta. This malefactor enticed the courtezan Vasantasena into the deserted old garden Pushpakaranda, and for a mere trifle murdered her by strangling. He was taken with the booty, and confessed his guilt. Therefore are we under orders from King Palaka to execute him. And if any other commit such a crime, accursèd in this world and the next, him too King Palaka condemns to the like punishment.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Despondently. Aside._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: By hundred sacrifices purified, My radiant name Was once proclaimed by countless altars' side, And knew no blame. Now comes my hour of death, and evil men Of baser fame In public spots proclaim it once again, But linked with shame. 12
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_He looks up and stops his ears._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Vasantasena! Oh, my belovèd! From thy dear lips, that vied with coral's red, Betraying teeth more bright than moonbeams fair, My soul with heaven's nectar once was fed. How can I, helpless, taste that poison dread, To drink shame's poisoned cup how can I bear? 13
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ Out of the way, gentlemen, out of the way!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: This treasure-house, with pearls of virtue stored, This bridge for good men o'er misfortune's river, This gem now robbed of all its golden hoard, Departs our town to-day, departs forever. 14
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END
ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Whom fortune favors, find That all the world is kind; Whose happy days are ended, Are rarely thus befriended. 15
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Looks about him._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Their faces with their garments' hem now hiding, They stand afar, whom once I counted friends: Even foes have smiles for men with Fortune biding: But friends prove faithless when good fortune ends. 16
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ They are out of the way. The street is cleared. Lead on the condemned criminal.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Sighing._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: My friend Maitreya! Oh, this cruel blow! My wife, thou issue of a spotless strain! My Rohasena! Here am I, laid low By sternest fate; and thou, thou dost not know That all thy childish games are played in vain. Thou playest, heedless of another's pain! (ix. 29)
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Voices behind the scenes._ My father! Oh, my friend!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Listens. Mournfully._] You are a leader in your own caste. I would beg a favor at your hands.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ From _our_ hands you would receive a favor?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Heaven forbid! Yet a headsman is neither so wanton nor so cruel as King Palaka. That I may be happy in the other world, I ask to see the face of my son.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ So be it.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _A voice behind the scenes._ My father! oh, my father! [_Charudatta hears the words, and mournfully repeats his request._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Headsmen._ Citizens, make way a moment. Let the noble Charudatta look upon the face of his son. [_Turning to the back of the stage._] This way, sir! Come on, little boy!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_Enter Maitreya, with Rohasena._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Maitreya._ Make haste, my boy, make haste! Your father is being led to his death.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Rohasena._ My father! oh, my father!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Maitreya._ Oh, my friend! Where must I behold you now?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Perceives his son and his friend._] Alas, my son! Alas, Maitreya! [_Mournfully._] Ah, woe is me!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Long, too long, shall I thirst in vain Through all my sojourn dread; This vessel small will not contain The water for the dead. 17
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: What may I give my son? [_He looks at himself, and perceives the sacrificial cord._] Ah, this at least is mine.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: The precious cord that Brahmans hold Is unadorned with pearls and gold; Yet, girt therewith, they sacrifice To gods above and fathers old. 18
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_He gives Rohasena the cord._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Goha._ Come, Charudatta! Come, man!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Ahinta._ Man, do you name the noble Charudatta's name, and forget the title? Remember:
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: In happy hours, in death, by night, by day, Roving as free as a yet unbroken colt, Fate wanders on her unrestricted way. 19
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Life will depart his body soon; Shall our reproaches bow his head? Although eclipse may seize the moon, We worship while it seems but dead. 20
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Rohasena._ Oh, headsmen, where are you leading my father?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END
ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ My darling,
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: About my neck I needs must wear The oleander-wreath; Upon my shoulder I must bear The stake, and in my heart the care Of near-approaching death. I go to-day to meet a dastard's ending, A victim, at the fatal altar bending. 21
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Goha._ My boy,
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Not we the headsmen are, Though born of headsman race; Thy father's life who mar, These, these are headsmen base. 22
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Rohasena._ Then why do you murder my father?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Goha._ Bless you, 't is the king's orders must bear the blame, not we.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Rohasena._ Kill me, and let father go free.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Goha._ Bless you, may you live long for saying that!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Tearfully embracing his son._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: This treasure--love--this taste of heaven, To rich and poor alike is given; Than sandal better, or than balm, To soothe the heart and give it calm. 23
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_Enter Sthavaraka, fettered, in the palace tower._]

text: _Sthavaraka._ [_After listening to the proclamation. In distress._] What! the innocent Charudatta is being put to death? And my master has thrown me into chains! Well, I must shout to them.--Listen, good gentlemen, listen! It was I, wretch that I am, who carried Vasantasena to the old garden Pushpakaranda, because she mistook my bullock-cart for another. And then my master, Sansthanaka, found that she would not love him, and it was he, not this gentleman, who murdered her by strangling.--But they are so far away that no one hears me. What shall I do? Shall I cast myself down? [_He reflects._] If I do, then the noble Charudatta will not be put to death. Yes, through this broken window I will throw myself down from the palace tower. Better that I should meet my end, than that the noble Charudatta should perish, this tree of life for noble youths. And if I die in such a cause, I have attained heaven. [_He throws himself down._] Wonderful! I did not meet my end, and my fetters are broken. So I will follow the sound of the headsmen's voices. [_He discovers the headsmen, and hastens forward._] Headsmen, headsmen, make way!

text: I ate a shour and bitter dish Of meat and herbs and shoup and fish; I tried at home my tongue to tickle With rice-cakes plain, and rice with treacle. 29
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_He listens._] The headsmen's voices! They shound like a broken brass cymbal. I hear the music of the fatal drum and the kettle-drums, and sho I shuppose that that poor man, Charudatta, is being led to the place of execution. I musht go and shee it. It is a great delight to shee my enemy die. Beshides, I 've heard that a man who shees his enemy being killed, is sure not to have shore eyes in his next birth. I acted like a worm that had crept into the knot of a lotush-root. I looked for a hole to crawl out at, and brought about the death of thish poor man, Charudatta. Now I 'll climb up the tower of my own palace, and have a look at my own heroic deeds. [_He does so and looks about._] Wonderful what a crowd there is, to shee that poor man led to his death! What would it be when an arishtocrat, a big man like me, was being led to his death? [_He gazes._] Look! There he goes toward the shouth, adorned like a young shteer. But why was the proclamation made near my palace tower, and why was it shtopped? [_He looks about._] Why, my shlave Sthavaraka is gone, too. I hope he has n't run away and betrayed the shecret. I musht go and look for him. [_He descends and approaches the crowd._]

text: _Charudatta._ Who are you, unselfish friend?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Monk._ You do not remember me, sir. I am that shampooer, who once was happy to rub your feet. When I fell into the hands of certain gamblers, this sister in Buddha, upon hearing that I had been your servant, bought my freedom with her jewels. Thereupon I grew tired of the gambler's life, and became a Buddhist monk. Now this lady made a mistake in her bullock-cart, and so came to the old garden Pushpakaranda. But when that unworthy wretch learned that she would not love him, he murdered her by strangling. And I found her there.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Loud voices behind the scenes._
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Unending victory to Shiva be, Who Daksha's offering foiled; And victory may Karttikeya see, Who Krauncha smote and spoiled;
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: And victory to Aryaka the king-- His mighty foe he kills-- Far over all the earth's expansive ring, That earth her joyous flag abroad may fling, The snowy banner of Kailasa's hills. 45
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_Enter hurriedly Sharvilaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Yes, Palaka, the royal wretch, I slew, Anointing Aryaka good king and true; And now, like sacrificial flowers, I wed The king's commandment to my bended head, To give sad Charudatta life anew. 46
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: The foe whose powers and friends had fled, he slew, Consoled and comforted his subjects true; And earth's broad sovereignty has gladly wed His power, and bent to him her lowly head, Who toward his foe plays Indra's part anew. 47
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_He looks before him._] Ah! There he will be found, where the people are thus gathered together. Oh, that this deed of King Aryaka might be crowned with the rescued life of noble Charudatta! [_He quickens his steps._] Make way, you rascals! [_He discovers Charudatta. Joyfully._] Is Charudatta yet living, and Vasantasena? Truly, our sovereign's wishes are fulfilled.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Now, thanks to heaven, from sorrow's shoreless sea I see him saved by her he loved, set free By that sweet bark, that knew her course to steer With virtue's tackle and with goodness' gear. He seems the moon, whose light shines clear at last, When all the sad eclipse is overpast. 48
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Yet how shall I approach him, who have so grievously sinned against him? But no! Honesty is always honorable. [_He approaches and folds his hands. Aloud._] O noble Charudatta!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Who are you, sir?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END
ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: I forced your house in manner base, And stole the gems there left behind; But though this sin oppress my mind, I throw myself upon your grace. 49
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Not so, my friend. Thereby you showed your faith in me. [_He embraces him._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ And one thing more:
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: The very noble Aryaka, To save his family and name, Has slain the wretched Palaka, A victim at the altar's flame. 50
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ What say you?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: 'T was your cart helped him on his way, Who sought the shelter of your name; He slew King Palaka to-day, A victim at the altar's flame. 51
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Sharvilaka, did you set free that Aryaka, whom Palaka took from his hamlet, and confined without cause in the tower?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ I did.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ This is indeed most welcome tidings.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Scarcely was your friend Aryaka established in Ujjayini, when he bestowed upon you the throne of Kushavati, on the bank of the Vena. May you graciously receive this first token of his love. [_He turns around._] Come, lead hither that rascal, that villain, the brother-in-law of the king!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Voices behind the scenes._ We will, Sharvilaka.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Sir, King Aryaka declares that he won this kingdom through your virtues, and that you are therefore to have some benefit from it.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ The kingdom won through my virtues?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Voices behind the scenes._ Come on, brother-in-law of the king, and reap the reward of your insolence. [_Enter Sansthanaka, guarded, with his hands tied behind his back._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sansthanaka._ Goodnessh gracious!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: It came to pass, I ran away Like any ass, and had my day. They drag me round, a prishoner, As if they 'd found a naughty cur. 52
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_He looks about him._] They crowd around me, though I 'm a relative of the king's. To whom shall I go for help in my helplesshnessh? [_He reflects._] Good! I 'll go to the man who gives help and shows mercy to the shuppliant. [_He approaches._] Noble Charudatta, protect me, protect me! [_He falls at his feet._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Voices behind the scenes._ Noble Charudatta, leave him to us! let us kill him!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sansthanaka._ [_To Charudatta._] O helper of the helplessh, protect me!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ [_Mercifully._] Yes, yes. He who seeks protection shall be safe.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Impatiently._] Confound him! Take him away from Charudatta! [_To Charudatta._] Tell me. What shall be done with the wretch?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Shall he be bound and dragged until he dies? Shall dogs devour the scoundrel as he lies? If he should be impaled, 't would be no blunder, Nor if we had the rascal sawn asunder. 53
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Will you do as I say?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ How can you doubt it?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sansthanaka._ Charudatta! Mashter! I sheek your protection. Protect me, protect me! Do shomething worthy of yourshelf. I 'll never do it again!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Voices of citizens behind the scenes._ Kill him! Why should the wretch be allowed to live?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [_Vasantasena takes the garland of death from Charudatta's neck, and throws it upon Sansthanaka._]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sansthanaka._ You shlave-wench, be merciful, be merciful! I 'll never murder you again. Protect me!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Come, take him away! Noble Charudatta, say what shall be done with the wretch.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Will you do as I say?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ How can you doubt it?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Really?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Really.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Then let him be immediately--
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Killed?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ No, no! Set free.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ What for?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: The humbled foe who seeks thine aid, Thou mayst not smite with steely blade--
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ All right. We will have the dogs eat him alive.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ No, no!
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Be cruelty with kindness paid. 54
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Wonderful! What shall I do? Tell me, sir.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Why, set him free.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ It shall be done.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sansthanaka._ Hooray! I breathe again. [_Exit, with the guards._
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Mistress Vasantasena, the king is pleased to bestow upon you the title "wedded wife."
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Vasantasena._ Sir, I desire no more.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ [_Places the veil upon Vasantasena. To Charudatta._] Sir, what shall be done for this monk?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Monk, what do you most desire?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Monk._ When I see this example of the uncertainty of all things, I am twice content to be a monk.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ His purpose is not to be changed, my friend. Let him be appointed spiritual father over all the monasteries in the land.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ It shall be done.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Monk._ It is all that I desire.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Vasantasena._ Now I am indeed brought back to life.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ What shall be done for Sthavaraka?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Let the good fellow be given his freedom. Let those headsmen be appointed chiefs of all the headsmen. Let Chandanaka be appointed chief of all the police in the land. Let the brother-in-law of the king continue to act exactly as he acted in the past.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ It shall be done. Only _that_ man--leave him to me, and I 'll kill him.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: He who seeks protection shall be safe. The humbled foe who seeks thine aid, Thou mayst not smite with steely blade. Be cruelty with kindness paid. (54)
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Sharvilaka._ Then tell me what I may yet do for you.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: _Charudatta._ Can there be more than this?
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: I kept unstained my virtue's even worth, Granted my enemy his abject suit; Friend Aryaka destroyed his foeman's root, And rules a king o'er all the steadfast earth.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: This dear-loved maiden is at last mine own, And you united with me as a friend. And shall I ask for further mercies, shown To me, who cannot sound these mercies' end? 58
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Fate plays with us like buckets at the well, Where one is filled, and one an empty shell, Where one is rising, while another falls; And shows how life is change--now heaven, now hell. 59
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: Yet may the wishes of our epilogue be fulfilled.
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [Footnote 85: That is, the lightning.]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [Footnote 86: Rohasena is himself conceived as the receptacle of the water which a son must pour as a drink-offering to his dead father.]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [Footnote 87: The Manes or spirits of the blessèd dead.]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: [Footnote 88: A token of honorable marriage. Compare page 66.]
chapter_title: ACT THE TENTH: THE END

text: May kine yield streaming milk, the earth her grain, And may the heaven give never-failing rain, The winds waft happiness to all that breathes, And all that lives, live free from every pain.
chapter_title: EPILOGUE: Bharatavakya

text: In paths of righteousness may Brahmans tread, And high esteem their high deserving wed; May kings in justice' ways be ever led, And earth, submissive, bend her grateful head. 60
chapter_title: EPILOGUE: Bharatavakya

text: [_Exeunt omnes._]
chapter_title: EPILOGUE: Bharatavakya
